The primary endpoint is the cost per message to deliver 100% of the messages (hash bits, plus a 2-byte negative acknowledgement and the raw text when the first attempt fails), paired against an in-domain PPM order-1 sender. The hash-only sender delivered 857 of 1,000 messages on the first attempt and cost 192.8 bits per message, 18.4 bits more than PPM order 1 (95% bootstrap interval 10.9 to 26.3); by the pre-registered rule it spends more and is not equivalent within one byte. As secondary results we map measured sender memory against bits. The hash-only sender (8,190 B on a host build, keyed BLAKE2b tag included, as in every method) was the cheapest point in bits from 8,190 B up to, but excluding, PPM order 1 at 24,844 B, 45 to 46 bits below smaz2 and Unishox2; from PPM order 1 upwards, in-domain senders spend fewer bits, except order 2 pruned to 16 KiB. In airtime it loses to PPM order 1 on all five links priced, to Unishox2 on four, and to raw text with a tag on two, because each failure costs an acknowledgement frame and a fallback frame. A wider receiver search recovers half of the failures and makes the cost 7.7 bits lower than PPM order 1, at about three minutes of receiver time per failure, and still loses in airtime on four of five links. We report the measurement as a delimitation, with every deviation of the run.

papers.title: Deformations and Local Geometry of Lie Triple System Morphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, first we study the deformations, stability and rigidity of Lie triple system morphisms by means of higher derived brackets and augmented Yamaguti cohomology. The vanishing of the first cohomology gives formal and local inner rigidity. The vanishing of the second cohomology removes the formal extension obstructions and, in finite dimension over $\mathbb{R}$, gives local smoothness and stability under simultaneous perturbations of the two products. Next, we establish the relationship with Lie algebra homomorphisms in each part of the theory. The universal enveloping Lie algebra identifies a Lie triple morphism with a grading-preserving Lie homomorphism. We obtain the corresponding first cohomology isomorphism, the equivalence of formal and smooth deformations, and a stability result for graded Lie bracket perturbations. For Lie triple products induced by binary Lie brackets, we construct a comparison of differentials and obstruction classes. Under perfectness and a zero-centralizer condition, the local morphism spaces coincide. Finally, we relate triple subsystem graphs to graded Lie subalgebra graphs and compare their normal differentials.

papers.title: Efficient iterative methods for the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary condition
papers.authors: Salma Raiouadi, Mohamed El Alaoui Talibi, Mouna Hilal
papers.abstract: In this study, we present a comparison of iterative methods for the compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary conditions, based on a fully compressible cavitation model for lubricated bearings. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the two-dimensional problem. We introduce the Kirchhoff transformation to reformulate the nonlinear density-pressure relationship into a quasi-linear problem. We develop an efficient numerical approach to solve the two-dimensional nonlinear problem. The methods examined are the Gauss-Seidel method, the Newton-Raphson method and parallelized nonlinear Jacobi method, applied to one- and two-dimensional slider bearing configurations. The overall solution time is shown to depend strongly on the choice of method.

papers.title: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
papers.abstract: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^{\alpha}(u-u_0) = \Delta u^m$, $0<\alpha<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\frac{\alpha}{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-\Delta S^m = u_0/\Gamma(1-\alpha)$. Moreover, we show that $t^\alpha u^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $\alpha=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.

papers.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
papers.authors: Igor M. L. Pataro, Martina Mammarella, Fabrizio Dabbene, Teodoro Alamo
papers.abstract: This paper presents a deterministic geometric procedure for analysing affine constraints over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by chance-constrained set approximation. Analytical tests classify inequalities as always violated, never violated, or cutting. Pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be strictly violated at a common point, yielding a compatibility matrix. The tests follow from quadratic optimisation and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions, with explicit treatment of tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate inequalities. The formulation applies in arbitrary finite dimensions and provides geometric information for subsequent bounds on simultaneous sampled violations and safe-region approximation.

papers.title: Finitely Presented Covers of Topological Full Groups
papers.abstract: Commutator subgroups of infinite minimal subshifts provide the first examples of infinite, finitely generated, simple amenable groups. We prove that if $G$ is a finitely presented group which maps onto the commutator subgroup of the topological full group of an infinite minimal subshift, then $G$ contains a non-abelian free subgroup. This in particular implies that these groups are not finitely presented. We also show that the topological full group of an irreducible subshift of finite type contains non-abelian free subgroups.

papers.title: Pure mapping class group fixed points in $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$
papers.authors: Samuel Bronstein, Thomas Le Fils, Arnaud Maret
papers.abstract:
We classify all the fixed points for the action of the pure mapping class group on $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$ character varieties of surface groups. Up to trivial peripheral monodromies, we prove that the irreducible fixed points are either pair of pants representations, or restrictions of reduced Burau representations to a once-punctured torus and restrictions of reduced Gassner representations to a 4-punctured sphere. On the other hand, we prove that the only non-trivial reducible fixed points appear in genus 0 where they map all but at most three peripheral loops in the centralizer of the image, and in genus 1 where they are valued in the quaternion group $H_8$.
  As consequences, we deduce (i) that an irreducible representation in genus 0 with at least four non-trivial peripheral monodromies is rigid if and only if it is a fixed point, and (ii) a partial classification of irreducible representations of pure braid groups into $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$.

papers.title: Analytic information encoded in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of genus-one plane branches
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula recovering the Zariski invariant of a plane branch with one Puiseux pair from its Bernstein-Sato polynomial. Thus the Bernstein-Sato stratification refines the Zariski-invariant stratification. We determine the generic roots in each stratum from the value semigroup and the Zariski invariant, refining Yano's description for a fixed topological class. We also compute the maximal spectral-exponent discrepancy and relate it to the dimension of the generic Bernstein-Sato locus and the minimum Tjurina number.

papers.title: Unconditional Uniqueness of KdV and mKdV Green Solutions at Low Regularity
papers.abstract: We prove unconditional uniqueness for the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation in $C_tH^{-1}_x(\mathbb R)$ and the real defocusing modified KdV equation in $C_tL^2_x(\mathbb R)$ within the class of Green solutions, an intrinsically well defined solution notion that encodes the evolution at these low regularities through the diagonal Green functions of the associated Lax operators. A key contribution is automatic local smoothing: the Green identities imply $q\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for KdV and $u_x,u^2\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for mKdV in spacetime, with estimates uniform over spatial translates. The uniqueness results therefore identify every Green solution in these classes with the continuous extension of the corresponding Schwartz flow.

papers.title: Directed systems of A-spaces and weak cores
papers.abstract: We prove that for any regular CW-complex $X$ there exists a quotient map $X\to Y$ that is a weak homotopy equivalence and which is minimal with that property, meaning that any quotient $Y\to Z$ that is a weak equivalence, must be a homeomorphism. The space $Y$ we obtain is an Alexandroff space: a space in which arbitrary intersections of open sets are open. The weak core $Y$ of $X$ is not unique in general. We study homotopy invariants preserved by filtered colimits of Alexandroff spaces. This can be seen as an analogous to Stong's theory of cores of finite topological spaces.

papers.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<\alpha<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. By combining inverse-stable subordination with global bounds for the hyperbolic heat kernel, we distinguish a short-time local regime, a large-time interior region, and an exterior region governed by a saddle-point problem with parameter $r/t$. Both kernels have the same exterior exponential rate, while their amplitudes are related by an explicit saddle-point factor. The estimates are uniformly comparable on the interfaces between regimes, recover the Euclidean time-fractional singularities at small scales, and identify the influence of hyperbolic geometry on large-scale decay. The kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}$ also describes the one-time marginal density of hyperbolic Brownian motion under an independent inverse stable clock. This representation yields a radial limit law, moment and quantile asymptotics, and a change in the mean square displacement from order $t^\alpha$ at small times to order $t^{2\alpha}$ at large times.

papers.title: Near-Riesz and pseudo-Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules and semi-C*-Fredholm operators
papers.abstract: Several useful concepts of almost frames or Riesz bases of Hilbert spaces gave us the motivation to review the theory of C*-module frames and C*-module Riesz bases for Hilbert C*-modules, searching for similar useful structures. We give a survey of the background in C*-module frame theory, summarizing and particularly extending or correcting earlier results. The concepts of near-Riesz bases, pseudo-frames, pseudo-Riesz sequences, and pseudo Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules are introduced and equivalently related to (semi-)C*-Fredholm properties of their synthesis operators. The notion of the excess of a C*-module frame is introduced, taking values in related C* algebras. Indicators for possible erasures of frame elements are described with the aim to preserve robustness of frames. Introducing a new notion of pseudo-Riesz-Weyl sequences in the standard Hilbert C*-module $l_2(A)$ we reverse the found correspondence by assuming the associated synthesis operator of a Bessel sequence to be (upper semi-)C*-Weyl. Furthermore, we deduce from the invariance of (upper semi-)C*-Fredholm and C*-Riesz-Weyl properties of synthesis operators with respect to ''compact'' perturbations the perturbation invariance of the respective classes of module Bessel sequences.

papers.title: A generalized Saito criterion, from line arrangements to curves
papers.abstract:
We formulate a generalized Saito criterion for complex projective plane curves, building on
  a recent generalized Saito criterion for plus-one generated arrangements of hyperplanes due to Junyan Chu.

papers.title: FasterRW: An Efficient Prior-Assisted Random Walk Solver for Thermal Analysis
papers.authors: Zixiao Wang, Tianshu Hou, Chenghan Wang, Zhen Zhuang, Leilei Jin, Tsung-Yi Ho, Farzan Farnia, Bei Yu
papers.abstract: Thermal simulation is becoming increasingly critical in modern IC design and manufacturing. Feynman--Kac random walk methods can estimate localized temperatures without solving the global field, but in practical settings without Dirichlet boundaries they require very long paths to control the truncation residual. This paper presents FasterRW, a continuation-value framework for accelerating Feynman--Kac thermal random walks. We prove a stopping-time residual identity showing that the expected tail after truncation equals the current attenuation weight multiplied by the temperature at the stopping location. This identity enables a prior-corrected single-point estimator: a cheap, noisy prior replaces the unknown continuation value, making the truncation bias scale with prior error rather than absolute temperature and yielding an error-controlled threshold-selection rule. For multi-point queries, FasterRW further converts cross-query pass-through tails into pseudo-samples and refines the resulting observations in prior-error coordinates through kriging. Compared with prior state-of-the-art methods, FasterRW achieves up to $28\times$ acceleration while maintaining accuracy. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/ShiningSord/FastRW.

papers.title: Drift-admissibility via Optimal Transport
papers.authors: Abigail Langbridge, Enrico Biffis, Jakub Mare\v{c}ek, Robert Shorten
papers.abstract: We introduce structure-aware optimal transport diagnostics for assessing whether empirical time-series dynamics are compatible with a prescribed predictable-drift class. Our approach translates a pathwise property of stochastic processes into a finite-dimensional projection problem over empirical transition laws, encoding admissibility as row-wise moment constraints on local couplings and quantifying deviations via a Kullback--Leibler projection gap $G_{\lambda,k}$. This yields both a principled diagnostic and a scalable Bregman--Dykstra algorithm that retains the efficiency of Sinkhorn-type methods while incorporating structural constraints. Calibrated against a Brownian reference null, $G_{\lambda,k}$ separates process classes that are indistinguishable by second-order statistics alone---including fractional Brownian motion and BSS processes sharing identical Hurst indices---without asymptotic resampling or continuous-time recovery. This positions the method as a general tool for structure-aware model validation of sequential data.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Undirected Path, Chordal Bipartite, and Strongly Chordal Graphs
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper coloring in which each nonisolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether the clique number of colors suffices is NP-complete on undirected path graphs, even with a supplied representation by paths in a star. One extra color suffices on every instance in the reduction. We also prove NP-completeness on chordal bipartite graphs for every fixed palette size $k\ge4$. For strongly chordal graphs, reverse simple elimination gives a constructive upper bound of one more than the clique number. We obtain exact polynomial-time algorithms under several conditions on the maximum cliques, including when they induce a connected subtree of a clique tree. For strictly chordal graphs we characterize the optimum and construct an optimal coloring in $O(n+m)$ time, where $n$ and $m$ count the vertices and edges. For strongly chordal graphs with clique-tree separators of size at most $s$, we give an exact algorithm in $n^{2^{O(s+1)}}$ time, with no bound on the clique number.

papers.title: Bourgain's Theorem for a Union of Euclidean Metric Spaces
papers.authors: Dimitar Chakarov, Sepideh Mahabadi, Yury Makarychev, Ali Vakilian
papers.abstract: We study the distortion of embedding a union of $k$ Euclidean sets into Euclidean space. We show that a union of $k$ Euclidean sets can be embedded with distortion at most $O(k^{1.128} \log k)$, independent of the number of points. This is an exponential improvement over the previous best known upper bound of $2^{O(k)}$ obtained by iterating the result of Makarychev and Makarychev (2016) for the special case $k = 2$. Surprisingly, with the additional assumption that each Euclidean set remains Euclidean when we adjoin any other two points, we can obtain an asymptotically tight distortion of $O(\log k)$, thus, providing a generalization of Bourgain's Theorem (1985). Along the way, we also show that the distortion of the union can be upper bounded by $O(\log k)$ times the maximum of the Lipschitz extension constants of individual Euclidean sets.

papers.title: Genealogical Reinforcement in Branching Processes
papers.abstract: Within many ecological populations, survival and reproduction exhibit a dependence on social interactions with relatives. As one example, resource excess is often shared according to genealogical proximity. When viewed as a branching system, an individual's offspring distribution acquires an effective dependence on genealogical structure. In the specific case that a large, local family structure leads to a large set of offspring, this can be viewed as a form of genealogical reinforcement. To capture this mechanism, we introduce a branching model of finite-depth genealogical dependence. Given partial observations of this reproducing population and its genealogy, we would like to reject the hypothesis of independent branching and estimate the strength of dependence. We present a statistical framework for detection and estimation, combining analytical results with simulation-based validation. We then identify our branching model with a tree-valued multitype branching process on a finite type space, providing a rigorous characterization of the expected structural reinforcement. Finally, we discuss how these tree-valued interactions can be accommodated within a broader class of stochastic processes.

papers.title: Spiking neuromodulation: a linear control perspective
papers.abstract: Neuronal excitability is a nonlinear phenomenon, and the complexity of spiking experimental traces sometimes looks defeating. The present paper takes the view point that excitability is a neuromodulated property, and aims to demonstrate that the neuromodulation of spiking is amenable to the classical linear analysis tools of control theory. We illustrate the value of linear feedback analysis as an alternative to bifurcation analysis in the simple yet classical example of spiking modulation by the A-type potassium current.

papers.title: A Gamma-Mixture Solution for Definite Noncentral Complex Gaussian Quadratic Forms
papers.authors: Fernando D. Almeida Garc\'ia, Carlos R. Nogueira da Silva, Felipe A. P. de Figueiredo, Rausley A. A. de Souza, Michel Daoud Yacoub, Jos\'e C\^andido Silveira Santos Filho
papers.abstract: Finding exact solutions for the statistics of definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms (CGQFs) has long been a challenging problem. Among existing exact approaches, Raphaeli's formulation [1] remains the most computationally efficient. However, its analytical tractability is hindered by the dependence of its series coefficients on the evaluation variable, which confines their statistics to the probability density function (PDF) and cumulative distribution function (CDF). This paper overcomes this limitation by deriving novel Gamma-mixture representations for the PDF and CDF of positive- and negative-definite noncentral CGQFs. The resulting structure broadens Raphaeli's statistical framework beyond the PDF and CDF to a wider class of CGQF functionals and a substantial range of practical applications. In particular, expectations of integrable functions of definite noncentral CGQFs are expressed as weighted sums of the corresponding expectations over Gamma random variables, enabling the direct derivation of moments, transforms, and performance measures. Moreover, the proposed formulation reduces the single-point complexity from \(O\!\left(n^2K+nK^2\right)\) for Raphaeli's method to \(O\!\left(nK+K^2\right)\), where \(n\) denotes the quadratic-form dimension and \(K\) the truncation order. The proposed Gamma-mixture structure also enables closed-form approximations that, by construction, remain valid probability distributions for any truncation order. In addition, uniform PDF and CDF truncation-error bounds are derived, allowing prescribed-accuracy truncation. As a sample application, we derive the first reported exact average bit error rate expression for maximal-ratio combining receivers with an arbitrary number of branches under an arbitrary positive-definite Rician correlation structure.

papers.title: On Lipschitz Explosion in Deep Neural Networks with Normalization: Consequences for Optimization and Adversarial Robustness
papers.authors: Ashkan Soleymani, Reyhaneh Hosseinpourkhoshkbari, Hadi Daneshmand, Patrick Jaillet
papers.abstract: Can a network look stable at every layer and still be exponentially unstable as a whole? The Lipschitz constant of a neural network is a basic stability quantity appearing in optimization guarantees, generalization bounds, and robustness certificates. Deep networks naturally admit two such notions, input Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to data perturbations, and parameter Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to weight perturbations. We prove that, for deep networks with normalization layers, with batch normalization as the canonical example, both Lipschitz constants can grow exponentially with depth and hence with parameter dimension, even under strong per-layer norm control such as $\|W_\ell\|_2\le 1$, and already for linear activations. Thus, a mechanism widely used to stabilize training can create severe worst-case instabilities that are invisible locally, i.e., from layerwise norm bounds alone. Parameter-Lipschitz explosion turns Lipschitz-dependent nonsmooth optimization guarantees into exponential-in-dimension bounds for deep normalized networks, while input-Lipschitz explosion makes worst-case Lipschitz-based generalization and robustness certificates vacuous. The latter also yields a concrete rank-separation mechanism for adversarial vulnerability. The theory predicts that perturbations introducing new singular directions should be amplified much more strongly than perturbations at the same noise level that remain within the input's original singular subspace. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 support this prediction, showing that rank-creating perturbations cause substantially sharper drops in accuracy, confidence, and margins than same-subspace perturbations.

papers.title: Multi-Model Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Transceiver Beamforming and Device Grouping
papers.authors: Chong Zhang, Min Dong, Ben Liang, Ali Afana, Yahia A. Eldemerdash Ahmed
papers.abstract: This paper considers uplink communication design for training multiple independent machine learning models via wireless federated learning. To reduce communication delay, we utilize multi-antenna beamforming and propose a multi-model over-the-air (M-OTA) uplink transmission and aggregation method for simultaneous training of multiple models. Devices are formed into groups for local model training based on the model assignments per communication round and simultaneously perform OTA aggregation over a multi-access channel. Based on the M-OTA transmission and reception process, we formulate a joint optimization of transmit and receive beamforming and device grouping over $T$ communication rounds to maximize the training convergence rates of all models. We analyze the per-model optimality gap, which captures the impact of noisy aggregation and inter-model interference on the learning performance. We further show that the $T$-round joint optimization problem can be decomposed into per-round online optimization to devise solutions. Following this, we propose a device grouping strategy that explores channel correlation among devices to maximize OTA aggregation performance. Furthermore, we present a low-complexity iterative algorithm for joint transmit-receive beamforming with closed-form updates. Simulation shows that our proposed M-OTA approach substantially outperforms the conventional single-model sequential OTA approach and other commonly used beamforming schemes.

papers.title: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles
papers.authors: Boris Landa, Francesco Strino, Fabio Parisi, Ruiqi Li, Yuval Kluger
papers.abstract: Low-rank approximation is a basic tool for inference from large and noisy data matrices. However, when noise variances differ across entries, a setting known as heteroskedasticity, the noise can distort the observed spectrum, producing spurious components and obscuring weak signals. To address these challenges, we develop BRINE (Blind Resolvent-based Iterative Noise Equalizer), a data-driven procedure that iteratively rescales rows and columns to equalize the average noise variance across both dimensions. Under suitable conditions, this procedure restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum and can amplify signal components without prior knowledge of the signal or noise structure. A key idea underlying our approach is to equalize the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing the unknown noise variances. At the population level, we identify a potential function that characterizes this equalization and motivates an iterative minimization procedure. We prove convergence of the iterations to the true equalizer for arbitrary positive variance profiles, with a geometric rate under mild conditions. The updates can be estimated directly from noisy data, and we establish probabilistic error bounds for the scaling factors. Simulations and experiments across diverse biological data modalities and preprocessing pipelines illustrate the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
papers.authors: Saksham Jain, Guillaume Braun, Masaaki Imaizumi
papers.abstract: Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.

papers.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology
papers.abstract: In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the \(\varepsilon\)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the \(L_p\) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to the maximum-vertex rule,} allowing higher-dimensional simplices to enter the filtration after their boundary faces, whereas {LpF and SMF use aggregation functions that depend on all vertex values rather} than solely on their maximum. By modifying how filtration values are assigned, these methods allow simplices to enter the filtration more progressively, so that topological features such as loops and voids may persist over longer filtration intervals rather than being filled immediately. Consequently, the resulting persistence diagrams may include persistence features that are not observed under LSF, potentially providing useful information for distinguishing data populations. Experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed filtration methods are computationally efficient and can provide greater sensitivity to structural differences in the data than LSF.

papers.title: Containment Problems in Convex Sets
papers.authors: Prosenjit Bose, Bobby Miraftab, Tyler Tuttle
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases. When $C$ is strictly convex we achieve a fraction of $1/5$, and when $C$ is a general convex region we achieve a fraction of $1/6e$. We show how the ideas of this second bound can be used to prove a lower bound for a version of the problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $C$ is a $d$-ball. We also consider a few special cases. When $C$ is a triangle we get a lower bound of $1/12$, and when we allow that triangle to be rotated by $\pi$ radians in addition to being scaled and translated we get a lower bound of $1/768$. In proving this last result, we improve the state of the art on the version of this problem in three dimensions, where $C$ is a parallelepiped. We also consider the algorithmic aspects of finding such a pair of points.

papers.title: Synchronized Optimal Transport Reconstructs Coupled Transcriptomic and Chromatin Dynamics
papers.authors: Jingfeng Wang, Yanxiang Zhao, Qing Nie, Zixuan Cang
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA and ATAC data collected across developmental stages provide time-course snapshots of transcriptional and regulatory states. Since sequencing is destructive, trajectories between these snapshots must be inferred from independently sampled cell populations. Existing approaches typically infer continuous dynamics in a single modality or integrate RNA and ATAC in a shared representation. Here we present Cross-Omics Aligned Trajectory Inference (COATI), which extends unbalanced synchronized dynamical optimal transport to time-dependent cross-modal maps for reconstructing coupled trajectories in distinct RNA and ATAC state spaces. We evaluated COATI on synthetic benchmarks and four developmental datasets using held-out-stage reconstruction and lineage analyses. COATI improved reconstruction of cell populations at held-out stages, including recovery of chromatin-state heterogeneity within cell types, and better preserved developmental lineage relationships. The unbalanced formulation allows the inference of population mass changes, which were shown to associate with DNA-replication programs at early stages and lineage-maturation programs later in development. The coupled trajectories enabled analysis of lineage-specific transcriptional and chromatin changes and their temporal relationships during development. Lineage responses inferred by COATI agreed with independent CRISPR perturbation results, and the inferred regulatory patterns were consistent with independent epigenetic data.

papers.title: On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
papers.authors: Yaroslav Kivva, Aliaksandra Novik, Negar Kiyavash
papers.abstract: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.

papers.title: Supervised Factor-Augmented Matrix Regression with Weak Factors
papers.authors: Wenyan Hou, Zhaoxing Gao, Ruey S. Tsay
papers.abstract: We develop a supervised factor-augmented matrix regression framework for high-dimensional analysis with weak factors. When factor loadings are concentrated on unknown subsets of rows and columns, conventional full-matrix factor extraction may suffer substantial signal dilution, with weakness in one matrix dimension propagating to estimation in the other. We characterize this two-way weak-loading phenomenon for both \(\alpha\)-PCA and projected estimators and show that their loading and factor estimates may deteriorate under weak signals. To address this problem, we propose a sequential response-guided screening procedure that identifies informative rows and columns prior to factor extraction. We establish exact support recovery and show that post-screening factor re-estimation converts the weak-loading problem into a pervasive one relative to the retained dimensions, yielding sharper convergence rates under substantially weaker dimensional growth conditions and consistent factor-number determination. We further establish asymptotic distributions for both unrestricted and bilinear regression estimators based on the estimated matrix factors. Simulations demonstrate substantial improvements in support recovery and factor estimation under weak signals. We illustrate the gains obtained by the response-guided factor construction with two empirical applications.

papers.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
papers.abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

papers.title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
papers.authors: Wei Wang, Himanshu Sharma, Thiagarajan Ramachandran
papers.abstract: Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. Minute-level operational scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints, and incorporates a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to enhance flexibility. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

papers.title: Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
papers.abstract: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.

papers.title: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
papers.abstract:
The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from
  infrared divergences

papers.title: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
papers.authors: Sophie Hall, Heinrich H. Nax, Saverio Bolognani
papers.abstract: Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.

papers.title: Separating Measures by Hyperplanes
papers.authors: Jos\'e Correa, Svenja M. Griesbach, Elfarouk Harb, Felix Hommelsheim, Reda Jlibene, Vasilis Livanos, Eilon Solan
papers.abstract:
Given red and blue points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, connect every red point to every blue point and weigh each segment by its length under a fixed norm. What fraction of the total weight can always be captured by a single affine hyperplane separating the segments' endpoints? We study this question for finite point configurations in affine general position and, more generally, for pairs of probability measures.
  For dimension one, we show that choosing the best of three thresholds determined by the means of the two distributions captures at least one third of the total red-blue distance. We also give a matching upper bound. Embedding the line construction to higher dimensions shows that the guarantee of $1/3$ cannot be improved for arbitrary measures. Thus, we pivot to the family of measures whose atoms are in affine general position and whose non-atomic part places zero mass on all hyperplanes. Crucially, we establish that the worst-case guarantee is identical for finite configurations in affine general position and several natural classes of probability measures, thereby unifying the discrete and continuous formulations of the problem.
  For this family of measures and for higher dimensions, we extend our guarantee of $1/3$ for all norms. Our proofs combine the ham-sandwich theorem with a novel coupling argument and, in the planar case, an integral representation of norms. We also show that the optimal guarantee improves as the dimension grows, giving a lower bound of $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/\sqrt{d}\right)$ as well as an asymptotically matching upper bound of $1/2$ for every $d$. For the Euclidean distance, we refine the lower bounds to $8/(8+5\pi)$ and $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/d\right)$ and, for $d=2$, the upper bound to $5/11$. We also derive dimension-dependent guarantees for finite point configurations, including perfect separation of $n$ points of each color when $d\geq2n-1$.

papers.title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
papers.authors: Prahladh Harsha, Swastik Kopparty, Mrinal Kumar, Ramprasad Saptharishi, Madhu Sudan
papers.abstract:
We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial.
  The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $\epsilon$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $\epsilon$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/\epsilon$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set.In this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(\epsilon)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/\epsilon^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis.
  On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.

papers.title: Controlled Excitation for Identification of Nonlinear Systems with Saturated Outputs
papers.authors: Adel Malik Annabi (McTAO, LJAD), Jean-Baptiste Pomet (McTAO), Dario Prandi (L2S, CNRS), Ludovic Sacchelli (McTAO)
papers.abstract: We consider nonlinear systems whose measured output is the product of an unknown matrix and a known saturation function of the unmeasured state. Generating excitation that allows the matrix to be recovered from the output is challenging when the dynamics are largely unknown. We exploit saturation to construct this excitation. Under a geometric accessibility condition, we derive explicit open-loop controls that drive the state into regions where the saturation takes prescribed values. For componentwise saturations, this condition holds generically with as few as two independent control directions. The controls require no state measurement and only partial knowledge of the dynamics, with no information on the structure of its nonlinear part. The resulting regressor is known in advance, and the unknown matrix is recovered exactly by a closed-form regression. Under stronger structural assumptions and with sufficiently many independent outputs, an output feedback tracks prescribed reference trajectories within the unsaturated region to arbitrary accuracy and permits exact state recovery. Suitably chosen references then also enable exact identification of linearly parameterized (nonlinear) dynamics. We analyze robustness to measurement noise and illustrate the method numerically in the presence of both measurement and dynamical noise.

papers.title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
papers.authors: Charles Minier (CNP, LSAF), St\'ephane Loisel (CNAM Paris), Renata Alcoforado (UFPE, ULISBOA)
papers.abstract: Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. The proposed framework provides a transparent, reproducible tool for insurers to evaluate repair-policy levers and to align claims operations with decarbonisation targets while retaining an explicit stochastic risk perspective.

papers.title: Provable State Estimation with Recurrent Models
papers.authors: Vincent Andrieu (LAGEPP, CNRS), Pauline Bernard (CAS), Lucas Brivadis (L2S), Laurent Praly, Christian Wolf
papers.abstract: Estimating the state of a dynamical system from observations is a crucial task in robotics and control. Despite their empirical success, recurrent models often lack formal guarantees on convergence and robustness. We bridge this gap by analyzing these architectures from the perspective of nonlinear observer theory. By framing RNNs as a time-discretization of continuous latent dynamical systems (Neural ODEs), we demonstrate that enforcing a contraction condition on the latent flow guarantees the existence of a smooth, injective map of the true physical state into the latent space. We prove that this architecture acts as a tunable observer: by increasing a single scalar gain that scales the latent vector field, the estimation error can be driven to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of zero at an exponentially fast rate. We further establish quantitative bounds on the MLP complexity required to decode this latent state, and extend our formal guarantees to the discrete-time residual RNN implementation. We validate the theory on a real mobile robotic task, where a provably contracting model outperforms a vanilla GRU with substantially more stable training. We also report that unconstrained GRUs converge to contracting dynamics on this task, suggesting that contraction is an emergent property of well-trained sequence models.

papers.title: A Geometric Journey Through the Aharonov--Bohm Effect: Tonomura's Toroid, Pseudoscalar Phase, and Quantum Holonomy in Clifford Algebra
papers.abstract: The magnetic Aharonov--Bohm (AB) effect is often introduced through the idealised infinite solenoid and a complex scalar phase. We give a geometric-algebra formulation based on the compact toroidal magnets shielded by a superconductor employed in the electron-holography experiments of Tonomura and collaborators. Working in the real Euclidean Clifford algebra $ \mathrm{Cl}(3,0)$, we distinguish the unit volume pseudoscalar $I$ (grade 3), coordinate angles (scalars, grade 0), tangent vectors (grade 1), and directed surface bivectors (grade 2). The magnetic field is represented by the dual bivector $\mathcal{B}= I \mathbf B$, while the electromagnetic $U(1)$ phase is represented by the central unit multivector $e^{I\alpha}$ generated by the pseudoscalar $I$, rather than by a spatial rotor with a bivector generator. We establish the linked toroidal geometry, formulate magnetic flux and Stokes' theorem intrinsically in geometric algebra, and derive the holonomy element $U_\Gamma=\exp(Iq\Phi_B/\hbar)$ from $U(1)$ gauge covariance, with every sign fixed explicitly. We then express superconducting fluxoid quantization in the same notation and obtain the binary electron holonomy $U_\Gamma = (-1)^N$ in the ideal limit where the linked magnetic flux equals $N h/(2e)$. Finally, a short conditional-state description of the quantum source and field shows how a backreaction can introduce an additional phase and reduce interference visibility. The conditional-state overlap is represented by a central scalar--pseudoscalar element; preservation of the fluxoid sector alone does not guarantee unit coherence.

papers.title: Improved Approximation and Hardness Bounds for $\beta$-TSP
papers.authors: Paul Liu, Jack Spalding-Jamieson, Da Wei Zheng
papers.abstract: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) asks for a minimum-length Hamiltonian cycle in a complete weighted graph. Its approximability depends on the edge lengths: unrestricted instances admit no constant-factor approximation unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, metric instances admit Christofides' $3/2$-approximation, and fixed-dimensional Euclidean instances admit a PTAS. We study $\beta$-TSP, where the edge lengths satisfy $ \ell_{uw}\leq\beta(\ell_{uv}+\ell_{vw}) \qquad \forall\,u,v,w\in V\ \text{pairwise distinct}, \quad \beta\in\left[\tfrac{1}{2},1\right]. $ The condition arises naturally in various settings, for example, when metric travel times are combined with positive service times at the vertices. The previous best approximation algorithm, due to B\"ockenhauer et al., ranges from $1$ at $\beta=1/2$ to $3/2$ as $\beta$ approaches $1$. We obtain a strictly better guarantee for every $1/2<\beta<1$ by combining two simple constructions whose guarantees counterbalance each other. We also improve the best known approximation hardness bound for every $1/2<\beta<1$.

papers.title: M-Estimation in Censored Regression Model under Endogeneity
papers.authors: Swati Shukla, Subhra Sankar Dhar,  Shalabh
papers.abstract: This paper develops a general M-estimation framework for censored regression models under endogeneity. A two-stage estimation is proposed to address the issue of endogeneity in the first stage and the issue of censoring in linear regression models in the second stage. The issue of endogeneity is addressed via instrumental variables using the control function approach. The issue of censoring in linear regression models is addressed via M-estimation using a suitably defined class of loss functions yielding a class of estimators. Thus, the proposed general M-estimation framework nests several existing estimators as special cases for the respective loss functions. Moreover, this provides flexibility of accommodating a broad range of robust loss functions that have not previously been studied in the context of censored regression. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the proposed class of estimators. An empirical study based on simulated datasets is conducted to illustrate general M-estimation for various choices of loss functions and to examine the finite-sample performance of various resulting estimators.

papers.title: Mode interaction in inclined-layer convection: a physical interpretation
papers.authors: Zheng Zheng, Laurette S. Tuckerman, Tobias M. Schneider
papers.abstract: We carry out a numerical investigation of the Oberbeck--Boussinesq equations in a fluid layer inclined against gravity. Equilibria containing different numbers of co-rotating rolls are computed. Mixed-mode branches connect branches containing states with four and six identical co-rotating rolls. These branches display two contrasting routes to reducing (or increasing) the number of rolls, one in which rolls disappear (or appear) and another route in which rolls merge (or split). These results are interpreted in light of the $(2,3)$ mode interaction scenario.

papers.title: Solver-Free Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Edge Selection
papers.authors: Xinda Zheng, Frits de Nijs, Edward Lam
papers.abstract: Decision-focused learning trains prediction models to improve downstream decisions, but many methods require costly solver calls or optimal-solution labels. We propose a solver-free decision-focused learning framework for NP-hard edge-selection problems with uncertain parameters in the objective, the constraints, or both. A neural optimization layer is first trained without solution labels, using problem objectives and constraint penalties. Graph-informed edge scoring and iterative refinement encourage concentrated and structurally consistent continuous decisions. The layer is then frozen, and a prediction model is trained through its continuous output using a problem-specific loss evaluated under observed parameters. At deployment, the predictor, optimization layer, and a lightweight decoder produce decisions without solving the original NP-hard problem. Experiments on the asymmetric traveling salesperson and endpoint-free orienteering problems show consistently better decision quality than prediction-focused learning and improvements over most evaluated decision-focused baselines. Our framework requires less training time than the evaluated decision-focused baselines, even when optimization-layer pretraining is included. Neural deployment also produces decisions faster than solver-based deployment, offering a better quality-efficiency trade-off. The layer also reduces training cost in existing decision-focused methods when used as an approximate optimization oracle.

papers.title: Synchronization transitions in Kuramoto oscillators with mixed interactions
papers.authors: Abhishek Sharma, Ayushi Suman, Mehernaz Anvari, Manish Dev Shrimali, Charo I. del Genio, Sarika Jalan
papers.abstract: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic system for emergent synchronization phenomena, and significant efforts have been made to investigate its transition from incoherent to coherent dynamics. However, previous studies have almost exclusively assumed global coupling between the oscillators, even though many real-world systems are organized in specific network structures. Here, we fill this gap by examining finite-size effects in Kuramoto oscillator ensembles on networks with mixed-order interactions. Using numerical simulations, we show how parameters such as the size of the system, the average degree of the nodes and the strength of the interactions alter the behaviour of the transition to synchronization with respect to the known theoretical results that are derived for globally coupled infinite systems.

papers.title: Kernel-Based Learning of Analytic Operators and Parametric PDEs
papers.authors: Giovanni S. Alberti, Markus Holzleitner, Lorenzo Rosasco, Matteo Santacesaria
papers.abstract: We study kernel-based learning of analytic operators from finite samples, with a focus on how the regularity of the target should determine the choice of the kernel. We establish embeddings of analytic operators into vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and derive finite-sample, high-probability guarantees that quantify the uncertainty due to random sampling: in the noiseless setting, suitable analytic kernels yield rates exponential in a fractional power of the sample size, while Sobolev-type kernels yield polynomial rates. We apply the theory to the solution operator of a parametric elliptic PDE, where the training data are themselves finite-element approximations, and obtain bounds that separate the sampling and discretization contributions to the error and prescribe how the mesh size should be coupled to the sample size. The results are illustrated numerically.

papers.title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
papers.authors: Jadwiga Czy\.zewska, Tom\'a\v{s} Masa\v{r}\'ik, Marcin Pilipczuk, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski
papers.abstract:
Dallard, Milani\v{c}, and \v{S}torgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor.
  We revisit both conjectures. We show that the graphs used by Bonnet and Chang exclude much simpler planar graphs, including several $16$-vertex trees, and we introduce a second, independent family of hard instances. We also prove that $3$-Coloring is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in both settings, thus refuting the algorithmic conjecture in full, even in its quasipolynomial version, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{QP}$. On the structural side, we identify planar graphs $H$ for which the structural conjecture holds, while the algorithmic one fails. Thus, constantly dominated balanced separators cannot by themselves explain the tractability of Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring.

papers.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
papers.abstract: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.

papers.title: Tensor value and the 9/4 bound for matrix multiplication
papers.authors: Mahmut Levent Do\u{g}an, Vladimir Lysikov, Keiya Sakabe, Michael Walter
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent result that the exponent of matrix multiplication is at most 9/4 valid over every field. Our main tool is a fractional symmetrized variant of the tensor value introduced by Coppersmith and Winograd, used in place of spectral points (tensor characters) in the original proof. We prove a superadditivity inequality for a power of this value on partially direct sums, whose summands share one tensor factor and occupy independent subspaces in the other two. Together with the degenerations of polynomial multiplication tensors from the OpenAI proof, this inequality yields the bound.

papers.title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We propose a fixed-point acceleration method for optimization over probability measures, applicable to a variety of machine learning problems. We represent probability measures as pushforwards of a reference distribution through a neural network map and equip the parameter space with the induced pullback Wasserstein metric. This geometric structure allows natural gradient descent to be interpreted as a fixed-point iteration on a Riemannian manifold. We accelerate this iteration using Riemannian Anderson mixing method, which exploits historical residuals to capture approximate second-order information without forming Hessians. In the present parametric setting, the manifold is represented by Euclidean coordinates endowed with a point-dependent metric, simplifying retraction and vector transport. We evaluate the method on multimodal sampling, PDE-based inverse problems, aggregation dynamics, Bayesian logistic regression, and generative modeling. Across the tested tasks, Anderson mixing reduces the number of natural-gradient iterations and achieves competitive performance relative to SGD and Adam in terms of both loss-gradient evaluations and wall-clock time. These results suggest that fixed-point acceleration is an efficient tool for improving the computational efficiency of training on parametric Wasserstein methods.

papers.title: Remark on residual solutions in the $KBc$ algebra
papers.abstract: In this paper we study residual solutions of open bosonic string field theory in the $KBc$ algebra with the auxiliary identities $(\partial^mc)^2=0$ of the ghost field. These solutions are not covered by the classification based on the defining relations alone. We show that the operator which controls the cohomology on the residual family depends only on $s=\gamma_1+\gamma_2$. At positive level $n$, cohomology can appear only on the lines $s=\pm n$. We compute it through level four and find one class at every point of each line $s=-3$ and $s=-4$. These classes give exact polynomial deformations of the residual family. At level six on $s=-6$, the cohomology instead vanishes generically and has dimension two at $(-1,-5)$ and $(-5,-1)$. We also compute the failure of the standard generator redefinition to preserve the auxiliary identities, and discuss the regularization of an explicit residual solution.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
papers.authors: Oliver Dobson, Varun Jog, Chun Hei Michael Shiu
papers.abstract: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces. Both exact and approximate planning are known to be computationally hard in this setting, so prior work has explored natural assumptions that make planning easier. Recent work [Golowich et al., 2022] gave quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for observable POMDPs. These are POMDPs whose observation channels satisfy an $\ell_1$-observability condition, but notably, no assumptions are required on the transition dynamics. In a similar vein, for every fixed $\rho>0$, we give quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for $\rho$-decodable POMDPs. We show that decodability is implied by both $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-observability and is strictly weaker than observability. Moreover, we show that the optimal decodability constant can be computed in polynomial time, whereas computing the optimal $\ell_1$-observability constant is NP-hard in the worst case. We also show that the fast filter-forgetting guarantee underlying the approach of [Golowich et al., 2022] does not extend directly from $\ell_1$-observability to constant $\ell_2$-observability. Thus, decodability is an easy-to-check, unifying assumption under which quasipolynomial-time approximate planning for POMDPs is possible.

papers.title: Box-Cox Transformations of Correlation Matrices
papers.abstract: We consider Box-Cox transformations of correlation matrices, $\Phi_\alpha(C)=\mathrm{vecl}\{(C^{\alpha}-I)/\alpha\}$, with Jacobian $J_\alpha$. The family nests the raw correlations at $\alpha=1$, the generalised Fisher transformation (GFT), $C\mapsto\mathrm{vecl}(\log C)$, at $\alpha=0$, and the negated off-diagonal concentration coordinates at $\alpha=-1$. The inverse problem is a strictly convex program for every $\alpha$, so every member is injective. The map is onto $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, $d=n(n-1)/2$, if and only if $\alpha\le0$, such that $\alpha=0$ defines the boundary for unrestricted parametrizations. For $\alpha>0$ the image is bounded. The conditioning obeys the bound $\kappa(J_\alpha)\le\kappa(C)^{|1-\alpha|}$, where $\kappa(C)=\lambda_{\max}(C)/\lambda_{\min}(C)$, and on the surjective range the exponent is smallest at $\alpha=0$. Under Gaussian sampling with $n\geq3$, the asymptotic covariance of the transformed sample correlations is the identity at independence for every member, but only $\alpha=0$ retains the identity to first order in the correlations, whereas the leading joint third cumulant at independence vanishes only at $\alpha=1/3$. Finally, applying the transformation to the diagonal rescaling of $C$ that makes the result hollow adds a new family to the existing correlation parametrizations. For every $\alpha$ the rescaling solves a strictly convex problem and the inverse is explicit, and the scaled coordinates are unrestricted exactly when $\alpha=0$, where they recover the known global normal coordinates, centred at independence, for the efficient information metric of the correlations.

papers.title: On Superconformal Index Degenerations and Half-Indices in S-Confining Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We study the $p \rightarrow 0$ limit of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal indices and its relation to half-indices of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories. At the level of special functions, this limit reduces elliptic hypergeometric integrals to basic hypergeometric integrals. The scaling of the flavor fugacities determines the Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions of the chiral multiplets. The gauge multiplet has Neumann boundary conditions. We apply this prescription to s-confining theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$, $USp(2N)$, $G_2$, and $SU(N)$, and recover the half-index identities of several boundary confining dualities, expressed through the Nassrallah-Rahman and Gustafson integrals. For $SU(N)$ with a rank-two antisymmetric chiral, four fundamentals and $N$ antifundamentals, we obtain an analytic proof of the half-index identities proposed by Okazaki and Smith for all $N \geq 5$.

papers.title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
papers.authors: Alexander Michel, Jaroslav Scheinpflug, Xi Yin
papers.abstract: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$. We show that this operator agrees with the Hamiltonian on the ground-state subspace and has a spectral gap. For SU(2) specifically, the representation theory of the singlet sector gives an astronomical reduction in the number of degrees of freedom. This allows us to construct an efficient variational basis whose inner products we compute exactly. We demonstrate the method by computing a state that satisfies rigorous bounds on its energy $E\,g_{\mathrm{YM}}^{-2/3}\leq 4.18\times10^{-8}$ and ground-subspace overlap $\|P_{\ker H}\psi\|^2\geq 0.999997$. We compute ground-state moments with high precision, finding values consistent with the bounds from our matrix bootstrap. Additionally, the state accurately reproduces both the exponent and coefficient of the asymptotic radial probability density predicted by the three-graviton amplitude.

papers.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
papers.abstract: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schr\"odinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.

papers.title: Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
papers.abstract: Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. While they have fundamental theoretical implications, their existence has not been rigorously established. This is particularly subtle in the setting of the full infinite-dimensional bootstrap, i.e. the limit of zero numerical truncation. In this article, we prove that extremal solutions exist for OPE maximisation problems in 1d CFT. These are a large class of generically interacting, unitary, exact solutions of the crossing equation that maximise an OPE coefficient. We also prove that these problems have 'zero duality gap', meaning there exist functionals arbitrarily close to extremality. Our approach is to formulate the bootstrap as a convex optimisation problem in a Hilbert space and apply the Fenchel-Rockafellar theorem.

papers.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
papers.abstract: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, for a bounded connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ or in $C(\overline\Omega)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

papers.title: Convergence of iterated restricted mean values to harmonic functions
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain and let $\delta$ be a continuous positive function on $\Omega$ with $B(x,\delta(x))\subseteq\Omega$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $\sigma(f)(x)$ denote the average of $f$ over the ball $B(x,\delta(x))$. Restricted mean value theorems give conditions under which a fixed point of $\sigma$ must be harmonic. We study the dynamical counterpart of this question: the behavior of the iterates $\sigma^k(f)$. We show that for \emph{every} bounded domain and every bounded measurable $f$ that is continuous at the points of $\partial\Omega$, the iterates $\sigma^k(f)$ converge locally uniformly in $\Omega$ to the Perron--Wiener--Brelot solution of the Dirichlet problem with boundary values $f|_{\partial\Omega}$, and that the convergence is uniform on $\overline\Omega$ for all continuous $f$ if and only if $\Omega$ is regular for the Dirichlet problem. This contains and extends earlier results for $C^{2,\alpha}$ domains with $C^{2,\alpha}$ data and for strictly convex domains with continuous data. We also give explicit rates of convergence: an algebraic rate $O(1/k)$ on domains with a uniform exterior ball condition and a geometric rate on convex domains, when $\delta$ is comparable to the distance to the boundary.

papers.title: Line crossing problem for biased monotonic random walks in the plane
papers.abstract: A $\beta$-biased monotonic random walk in the plane moves from $(x,y)$ to $(x+1,y)$ or $(x,y+1)$ with probabilities $1/(\beta+1)$ and $\beta/(\beta+1)$. We study $\Phi_\beta(\alpha,d)$, the probability that the walk started at the origin ever visits a lattice point strictly above the line $y=\alpha x+d$, and $\Psi_\beta(\alpha,d)$, the probability that it visits a lattice point \emph{on} the line after leaving the origin. For integer slopes $\alpha=p$ we show $\Phi_\beta(p,d)=\rho^{\lfloor d\rfloor+1}$, where $\rho$ is the smallest positive root of $y^{p+1}-(\beta+1)y+\beta=0$, give the Fuss--Catalan series for $\rho$, identify $\rho$ with the extinction probability of a Galton--Watson process, and compute the exact law and mean of the first crossing point. We prove that the return probability is $\Psi_\beta(p,0)=(p+1)(1-\beta/((\beta+1)\rho))$, which equals $(p+1)/(\beta+1)$ for $\beta\ge p$. For rational slopes $\alpha=r/s$ we obtain $\Phi_\beta$ in closed form from the $s$ large roots of the kernel $\tfrac{\beta}{\beta+1}z^{r+s}-z^r+\tfrac1{\beta+1}$, and $\Psi_\beta$ as a ratio of Green's functions. For arbitrary real $\alpha$ we prove that the walk crosses every line $y=\alpha x+d$ almost surely if and only if $\beta\ge\alpha$, and we establish the two-sided bound $e^{-\theta(d+1)}\le\Phi_\beta(\alpha,d)<e^{-\theta d}$ with an explicit Lundberg exponent $\theta$. Finally, $\alpha\mapsto\Phi_\beta(\alpha,0)$ is a pure jump function: it is constant on $[0,\beta]$, continuous at every irrational point and has a jump at every rational $\alpha>\beta$.

papers.title: Integer matrices that are not copositive have certificates of less than quadratic complexity
papers.abstract: A real symmetric matrix is called copositive if the corresponding quadratic form is non-negative on the closed first orthant. If the matrix fails to be copositive there exists some non-negative certificate for which the quadratic form is negative. Due to the scaling property, we can find such certificates in every neighborhood of the origin but their properties depend on the matrix of course and are hard to describe. If it is an integer matrix however, we are guaranteed certificates of a complexity that is at most a constant times the binary encoding length of the matrix raised to the power 3/2.

papers.title: Dense semigroups of triangular matrices
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ be the semigroup of $n\times n$ lower triangular matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$. We show that $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ has dense subsemigroups generated by $n+1$ matrices, and that $n+1$ is the least possible number of generators; the same holds for dense subgroups of the group of invertible lower triangular matrices. The generators can be written down explicitly: $n$ of them are diagonal and one is a diagonal matrix plus a nilpotent perturbation. More precisely, let $D_0,\dots,D_m$ be diagonal matrices generating a dense subsemigroup of the diagonal matrices, where the diagonal entries of $D_0$ have strictly monotone moduli, and let $A$ be a lower triangular matrix with the same diagonal as $D_0$. We prove that the semigroup generated by $A,D_1,\dots,D_m$ is dense in $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ if and only if every subdiagonal entry of $A$ is nonzero.

papers.title: The Finite Difference Method, for the heat equation on Sierpi\'{n}ski simplices
papers.abstract: In the sequel, we extend our previous work on the Minkowski Curve to Sierpi\'{n}ski simplices (Gasket and Tetrahedron), in the case of the heat equation.
