First, we build the finite difference scheme. Then, we give a theoretical study of the error, compute the scheme error, give stability conditions, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Contrary to existing work, we do not call for approximations of the eigenvalues.

papers.title: On a characterization of spaces satisfying open mapping and equivalent theorems
papers.abstract: We study open-mapping, continuous-inverse and closed-graph properties for maps whose domain and range belong to the same class of Hausdorff topological vector spaces. Quotient and graph stability imply equivalence of these properties. In the locally convex setting, we characterize barrelled infra-Pt\'ak spaces and barrelled Pt\'ak spaces as largest classes determined by the closed-graph property, Banach test spaces and appropriate nearly-open image conditions.

papers.title: The maximal monotonicity of the subdifferential in locally convex spaces via upper envelopes
papers.abstract: We establish equivalent conditions for the convex subdifferential to be maximal monotone in general settings, expressed in terms of the associated upper envelopes.

papers.title: Scl in graphs of groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a group acting on a tree with cyclic edge and vertex stabilizers. Then stable commutator length (scl) is rational in G. Furthermore, scl varies predictably and converges to rational limits in so-called "surgery" families. This is a homological analog of the phenomenon of geometric convergence in hyperbolic Dehn surgery.

papers.title: Some ordering properties of highest and lowest order statistics with exponentiated Gumble type-II distributed components
papers.abstract: This paper studies stochastic comparisons of the highest and lowest order statistics arising from independent Exponentiated Gumbel Type-II distributed random variables. First, using vector majorization, we establish a comprehensive set of stochastic orderings for the lowest and highest order statistics with respect to the outer and inner shape parameters. In particular, for the lowest order statistic, we derive results on the usual stochastic order and likelihood ratio order, which further imply failure rate, mean residual life, and increasing convex orderings. Second, we show that the lowest order statistics satisfy a proportional failure rate structure. In addition, we also establish star and dispersive orderings. For the highest order statistic, we obtain results in the reversed failure rate order, and we show that, in general, a proportional failure rate structure does not hold. Moreover, unlike several classical exponentiated models, the highest order statistics are not necessarily comparable in the usual stochastic order under heterogeneity of the inner shape parameters. Finally, we extend the analysis using multivariate chain majorization to study the effect of simultaneous variation in scale and outer shape parameters. Under this framework, we establish usual stochastic ordering results for both the lowest and highest order statistics. It provides more general reliability comparisons under joint parameter heterogeneity.

papers.title: Periodic solutions of symmetric Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of periodic solutions of Hamiltonian system $\dot z(t)=J \nabla H(z(t))$, where $H$ is symmetric under an action of a compact Lie group. We are looking for periodic solutions in a nearby of non-isolated critical points of $H$ which form orbits of the group action. We prove Lyapunov-type theorem for symmetric Hamiltonian systems.

papers.title: Holed cone structures on 3-manifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce holed cone structures on 3-manifolds to generalize cone structures. In the same way as a cone structure, a holed cone structure induces the holonomy representation. We consider the deformation space consisting of the holed cone structures on a 3-manifold whose holonomy representations are irreducible. This deformation space for positive cone angles is a covering space on a reasonable subspace of the character variety.

papers.title: On the functoriality of the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms
papers.authors: Thomas Goodwillie, Kiyoshi Igusa, Cary Malkiewich, Mona Merling
papers.abstract: We construct an $(\infty,1)$-functor that takes each smooth $G$-manifold with corners $M$ to the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms ${\mathcal H}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$. We also give a stable analogue ${\mathcal H}^{\mathcal U}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$ where the manifolds are stabilized with respect to representation discs. The functor structure is subtle to construct, and relies on several new ideas. In the non-equivariant case $G=e$, our $(\infty,1)$-functor agrees with previous constructions of the smooth $h$-cobordism space as a functor to the homotopy category.

papers.title: Orders between channels and implications for partial information decomposition
papers.authors: Andr\'e F. C. Gomes, M\'ario A. T. Figueiredo
papers.abstract: The partial information decomposition (PID) framework is concerned with decomposing the information that a set of random variables has with respect to a target variable into three types of components: redundant, synergistic, and unique. Classical information theory alone does not provide a unique way to decompose information in this manner and additional assumptions have to be made. Recently, Kolchinsky proposed a new general axiomatic approach to obtain measures of redundant information, based on choosing a preorder relation between information sources (equivalently, a preorder between communication channels). In this paper, we exploit this approach to introduce three new measures of redundant information (and the resulting decompositions) based on well-known preorders between channels, thus contributing to the enrichment of the PID landscape. We relate the new decompositions to existing ones, study some of their properties, and provide examples illustrating their novelty. As a side result, we prove that any preorder that satisfies Kolchinsky's axioms yields a decomposition that meets the axioms originally introduced by Williams and Beer when they first propose the PID.

papers.title: Factorized $q$-difference equations and their fundamental solutions
papers.abstract: We construct fundamental solutions of a class of factorized $q$-difference equations in terms of Jacobi theta functions and Zwegers' $\mu$-functions. To obtain a formal series solution $f_0$ for a factorized $q$-difference equation, we present a $q$-analogue of the fundamental relation (often called the Wronski-type relation) between the elementary symmetric polynomials and the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials. We also provide some formulas for the image of the $q$-Borel summation of the formal series solution $f_0$. As an application, we give another proof of the expressions due to S. Y. Kang and S. P. Zwegers of the universal mock theta functions and higher level Appell functions in terms of $\mu$-functions.

papers.title: Automatic Synthesis of Low-Complexity Translation Operators for the Fast Multipole Method
papers.authors: Isuru Fernando, Chaoqi Lin, Andreas Kl\"ockner
papers.abstract:
The FMM is the leading approach for attaining linear complexity in the evaluation of long-range (e.g. Coulomb) many-body interactions. We demonstrate a new, hybrid symbolic-numerical method for the automatic synthesis of all families of translation operators required for the execution of the Fast Multipole Method (FMM). Our method is dimension-independent (demonstrated in 2D and 3D) and applicable to any translation-invariant kernel. Low complexity in translation operators for the FMM is usually achieved by algorithms specialized for a potential obeying a specific partial differential equation (PDE). Absent a PDE or specialized algorithms, Taylor series based FMMs or kernel-independent FMM have been used, at asymptotically higher expense.
  When symbolically provided with a constant-coefficient elliptic PDE obeyed by the potential, our algorithm can automatically synthesize translation operators requiring $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, where $p$ is the expansion order and $d$ is dimension, compared with $\mathrm{O}(p^{2d})$ operations in a naive approach carried out on (Cartesian) Taylor expansions. This is achieved by using a compression scheme that asymptotically reduces the number of terms in the Taylor expansion and then operating directly on this "compressed" representation. Judicious exploitation of shared subexpressions permits formation, translation, and evaluation of local and multipole expansions to be performed in $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, while an FFT-based scheme permits multipole-to-local translations in $\mathrm{O}(p^{d-1}\log(p))$ operations. We demonstrate computational scaling of code generation and evaluation as well as numerical accuracy through numerical experiments on a number of potentials from classical physics.

papers.title: A homotopical consequence of branched covers
papers.abstract: We prove that the profinite completion of a pseudomanifold is the Artin-Mazur's etale homotopy type construction on its branched covers, which was implicitly conjectured by Sullivan in his MIT note (page 272) around 1970. This is a consequence of the existence of enough $K(\pi,1)$ open dense subspaces in a pseudomanifold.

papers.title: Qin's Algorithm, Continued Fractions and 2-dimensional Lattices
papers.abstract: In his ``Mathematical Treatise in Nine Sections''(1247), Jiushao Qin introduced ``the Dayan method of deriving unity'' for computing modular inverses, an essential component of his treatment of the Chinese remainder theorem. A distinctive feature of Qin's algorithm is its use of a state consisting of four nonnegative integers arranged in a matrix. In this paper, we investigate the mathematical structure of these states and their connections with continued fractions and two-dimensional lattices. By introducing a signed version of the state, we obtain a natural matrix representation that reveals the convergents of continued fractions and gives direct derivations of several classical results. We then show that the signed states form bases of a family of two-dimensional lattices arising from modular congruences. In particular, we prove that a shortest lattice vector can be obtained from the rows of a signed state or their sum or difference. We also study the monotonicity of the inner products of the state vectors and discuss a subsequent result that locates a shortest vector in one of two consecutive states. It is surprising that a shortest lattice vector is found in a highly structure sequence of states. These results demonstrate that the state structure of Qin's algorithm provides a unified framework for understanding modular inversion, continued fractions, and shortest vectors in two-dimensional lattices.

papers.title: On local cohomology modules over ramified regular local rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show examples of local cohomology modules over ramified regular local ring, having finite set of associated primes. In doing so we consider our ramified regular local ring as Eisenstein extension of an unramified regular local ring sitting inside it. In ramified regular local ring for extended ideal (from the unramified one) set of associated primes of a local cohomology module is always finite. Using the Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence, we construct examples of local cohomology of non extended ideal, whose set of associated primes is finite. In particular, we choose those non extended ideals whose minimal primes are extended ideals which are all cohomologically complete intersection.

papers.title: A GL(3) converse theorem via a "beyond endoscopy" approach
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of the converse theorem for Maass forms on ${\rm GL}(3)$ using a technique that is inspired by Langlands' philosophy of "beyond endoscopy", thereby implementing these ideas for the first time in a higher rank setting.

papers.title: Triple product $p$-adic $L$-functions for finite slope families and a $p$-adic Gross-Zagier formula
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize two results of H. Darmon and V. Rotger on triple product $p$-adic $L$-functions associated with Hida families to finite slope families. We first prove a $p$-adic Gross-Zagier formula, then demonstrate an application to a special case of the equivariant Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for supersingular elliptic curves.

papers.title: Commutation relations for two-sided radial SLE
papers.authors: Ellen Krusell, Yilin Wang, Hao Wu
papers.abstract: We study the commutation relation for 2-radial SLE in the unit disc starting from two distinct boundary points. We follow the framework introduced by Dub\'{e}dat~[12]. Under an additional requirement of the interchangeability of the two curves, we classify all locally commuting 2-radial SLE$_\kappa$ for $\kappa\in (0,8)$: it is either two-sided radial SLE$_\kappa$ with spiral of constant spiraling rate or chordal SLE$_\kappa$ weighted by a power of the conformal radius of its complement. Namely, for fixed $\kappa$ and starting points, we have exactly two one-parameter families of locally commuting 2-radial SLE curves. We also discuss the semiclassical limit of the commutation relation as $\kappa \to 0$. In particular, we show that the limit for the second family with an appropriately chosen power of the conformal radius is a chord that minimizes a modified chordal Loewner energy, which is unique only when the endpoints are not antipodal.

papers.title: A uniform trigonometric R-matrix for the exceptional series
papers.abstract: The exceptional series is a finite list of points on a projective line with a simple Lie algebra attached to each point. This list of Lie algebras includes the five exceptional Lie algebras. We give a uniform trigonometric $R$-matrix for the exceptional series in the representation $L\oplus I$, where $L$ is the quantum deformation of the adjoint representation and $I$ is the trivial representation. We construct a sixteen dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit2)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^2(L\oplus I))$ and a 287 dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit3)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^3(L\oplus I))$. The $R$-matrix lives in $A^\square(\mathit2)$ and satisfies the Yang-Baxter equation in $A^\square(\mathit3)$; it interpolates the trigonometric $R$-matrices for the points in the exceptional series.

papers.title: Functional Extreme-PLS
papers.abstract: An extreme dimension reduction method is proposed, extending the Extreme-PLS approach to the discretized functional framework, where the covariate lies in the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space ($L^2([0,1])$) but is partially observed on a dense time grid. The ideas are partly borrowed from both Partial Least-Squares (PLS) and Sliced Inverse Regression (SIR) techniques. Accordingly, the method relies on the projection of the covariate onto a subspace and maximizes the covariance between its projection and the response conditionally on an extreme event capturing tail information. The covariate and the heavy-tailed response are supposed to be linked through a nonlinear inverse single-index model, and the objective is to infer the index in this regression framework. A new family of estimators is proposed, and its asymptotic consistency with convergence rates under the model is established. Assuming mild conditions on the noise, most of the assumptions are stated in terms of regular variation, unlike those commonly imposed for SIR and single-index regression. In addition, the theoretical analysis is expanded to include a model-free consistency result in probability for the empirical tail-moments in a general separable Hilbert space. Finally, the results are illustrated through a finite-sample study with synthetic functional data and high-frequency financial data, highlighting the effectiveness of the dimension reduction in capturing tail dependence and supporting extreme risk management.

papers.title: Best-Worst Disaggregation: An approach to the preference disaggregation problem
papers.authors: Matteo Brunelli, Fuqi Liang, Jafar Rezaei
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Best-Worst Disaggregation (BWD) method, a novel approach that integrates the principles of the Best-Worst Method (BWM) into the disaggregation framework to enhance the consistency and reliability of derived preference models. An optimization model is formulated to determine the most suitable additive value function that fits the preferences expressed by a decision-maker or expert. The method incorporates a consistency analysis to quantify and improve the reliability of the judgments and is extended to handle interval-valued preferences. We also developed an approach to identify a reference set, which is used for pairwise comparisons to elicit the value functions and weights. A case study in logistics performance evaluation demonstrates the practicality and effectiveness of BWD. By coupling a structured human-elicitation protocol with an inference engine and a consistency-feedback loop, BWD provides a human-centered building block for evidence-sensitive decision-support systems

papers.title: Matroid products via submodular coupling
papers.authors: Krist\'of B\'erczi, Bogl\'arka Geh\'er, Andr\'as Imolay, L\'aszl\'o Lov\'asz, Bal\'azs Maga, Tam\'as Schwarcz
papers.abstract:
The study of matroid products traces back to the 1970s, when Lov\'asz and Mason studied the existence of various types of matroid products with different strengths. Among these, the tensor product is arguably the most important, which can be considered as an extension of the tensor product from linear algebra. However, Las Vergnas showed that the tensor product of two matroids does not always exist. Over the following four decades, matroid products remained surprisingly underexplored, regaining attention only in recent years due to applications in tropical geometry and the limit theory of matroids.
  In this paper, inspired by the concept of coupling in probability theory, we introduce the notion of coupling for matroids -- or, more generally, for submodular set functions. This operation can be viewed as a relaxation of the tensor product. Unlike the tensor product, however, we prove that a coupling always exists for any two submodular functions and can be chosen to be increasing if the original functions are increasing. As a corollary, we show that two matroids always admit a matroid coupling, leading to a novel operation on matroids. Our construction is algorithmic, providing an oracle for the coupling matroid through a polynomial number of oracle calls to the original matroids.
  We apply this construction to derive new necessary conditions for matroid representability and establish connection between tensor products and Ingleton's inequality. Additionally, we verify the existence of set functions that are universal with respect to a given property, meaning any set function over a finite domain with that property can be obtained as a quotient.

papers.title: Twice Fourier transformable measures and diffraction theory
papers.authors: Hans G. Feichtinger, Christoph Richard, Christoph Schumacher, Nicolae Strungaru
papers.abstract: Mathematical diffraction theory has been developed since about 1995. Hof's initial approach relied on tempered distributions in euclidean space. Nowadays often the Fourier theory by Argabright and Gil de Lamadrid is used, which applies to appropriate measures on locally compact abelian groups. We review diffraction theory using Wiener amalgams as test function spaces. For translation bounded measures, this unifies and simplifies the former two approaches. We treat weighted versions of Meyer's model sets as examples.

papers.title: Generalised Buchberger and Schreyer algorithms for strongly discrete coherent rings
papers.authors: Henri Lombardi (LMB), Stefan Neuwirth (LMB), Ihsen Yengui
papers.abstract: Let M be a finitely generated submodule of a free module over a multivariate polynomial ring with coefficients in a discrete coherent ring. We prove that its module MLT(M) of leading terms is countably generated and give an algorithm for computing explicitly a generating set. This result is also useful when MLT(M) is not finitely generated. Suppose that the base ring is strongly discrete coherent. We provide a Buchberger-like algorithm and prove that it converges if and only if the module of leading terms is finitely generated. We also state a constructive version of Hilbert's syzygy theorem by following Schreyer's method.

papers.title: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology
papers.authors: Yairon Cid-Ruiz, Yupeng Li, Jacob P. Matherne
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi. We study the cohomology rings of complex varieties in terms of Macaulay inverse systems over $\mathbb{Z}$. As applications, we show that under certain conditions, the Macaulay dual generator is a denormalized Lorentzian polynomial in the sense of Br\"and\'en and Huh, and we give a characteristic-free extension (over $\mathbb{Z}$) of the result of Khovanskii and Pukhlikov describing the cohomology ring of toric varieties in terms of volume polynomials.

papers.title: Virtual double categories of relations relative to fibrations
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between virtual double categories and fibrations, or (hyper)doctrines, in the context of categorical logic. We present a construction that produces a virtual double category of relations internal to a fibration with finite products. We characterize the class of fibrations called elementary existential fibrations, a fibrational counterpart of regular logic, as those for which the induced virtual double category is a cartesian equipment. We also show that cartesian equipments arising in this manner are exactly those that satisfy the Frobenius axiom studied by Walters and Wood in the context of cartesian bicategories. Some logical principles, such as the comprehension axiom for predicates and the extensional equality predicate, are characterized as properties of the double categorical structure.

papers.title: Fluctuation Correction and Global Solutions for the Stochastic Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto System via Entropy-Based Regularization
papers.abstract: We study a stochastic extension of the n-species Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system, in which a multiplicative noise term accounts for fluctuation corrections to the mean-field dynamics arising from a finite underlying population. The noise we consider is motivated by, but not rigorously derived from, the particle-system approximation of Chen, Daus, Holzinger, and J"ungel; it only partially respects the entropy (gradient-flow) structure of the deterministic system, which is the main source of the technical difficulties addressed in this paper. For the resulting system of stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), we establish the existence of nonnegative, global, weak martingale solutions, under a detailed-balance condition on the diffusion coefficients and a smallness condition relating the noise intensity to these coefficients. This smallness condition amounts to a sufficiently large population size N (equivalently, small fluctuation strength 1/N): the existence theory thus operates in the perturbative regime around the deterministic mean-field limit, and for fixed coefficients it is always satisfiable once N is large enough.

papers.title: Kernel Metrics and Learning for Borel MDPs: Identifiability and Adaptive Control
papers.abstract: We consider a Markov decision process with standard Borel spaces and an unknown transition kernel under the average cost criterion. We do not impose any parametrization on the set of possible kernels. To facilitate our analysis, we first develop implication relations between several topologies on kernels defined by pointwise, continuous, or uniform weak convergence; we then review robustness properties on the space of kernels, and finally we establish compactness conditions on the space of kernels. Building on this regularity analysis, we then present two data-driven identifiability results; the first one being Bayesian and the second one empirical. Our conditions for the Bayesian setting are significantly more relaxed compared with prior work which considered either finite or parametric models, though we do not obtain a rate of convergence. Our analysis is asymptotic and builds on measurability in terms of the tail $\sigma$-field of the available information. Identifiability results are then used to design near-optimal adaptive control policies which alternate between periods of exploration, where the controller acts according to a policy which is conducive to the identification of the true kernel, and periods of exploitation where the controller's information on the kernel is utilized. We will establish that such policies are near optimal. In summary, our contribution is with regard to the general standard Borel setup where there is no apriori parametric representation.

papers.title: Equivalence of synchronization states in the Kuramoto flow: a unified framework
papers.authors: Ting-Yang Hsiao, Yun-Feng Lo, Chengbin Zhu
papers.abstract: On the fiftieth anniversary of the Kuramoto model, synchronization remains a central paradigm for collective behavior in complex oscillator systems. While phase locking, frequency synchronization, and order-parameter coherence are widely used to characterize synchronization, their precise dynamical relationship has remained unclear, especially in finite-dimensional systems beyond mean-field limits. In this work, we show that, in the fully connected Kuramoto model, full phase locking, phase locking, frequency synchronization, and order-parameter synchronization are dynamically equivalent. Moreover, we demonstrate that the equivalence between phase locking and frequency synchronization is governed by a topology-independent mechanism and persists for generic symmetric coupling structures. These results provide a unified dynamical framework for synchronization and clarify the structural role of the Kuramoto order parameter.

papers.title: On the regularity of entropy solutions to stochastic degenerate parabolic equations
papers.authors: Marko Erceg, Kenneth H. Karlsen, Darko Mitrovi\'c
papers.abstract: We study the regularity of entropy solutions for quasilinear parabolic equations with anisotropic degeneracy and stochastic forcing. Building on previous works, we establish space-time regularity under a non-degeneracy condition that does not require an assumption on the derivative of the symbol of the corresponding kinetic equation, a restriction imposed in earlier studies. This allows us to obtain regularity results for certain equations not accounted for by prior theory, albeit with reduced regularity exponents. Our approach uses a kinetic formulation with two transport equations, one of second order and one of first order, leveraging a form of "parabolic regularity" inherent in these equations that was not utilized in previous studies.

papers.title: A structure and asymptotic preserving scheme for the quasineutral limit of the Vlasov-Poisson system
papers.authors: Alain Blaustein (Centre Inria de l'Universit\'e de Lille), Giacomo Dimarco (Universit\`a di Ferrara), Francis Filbet (Universit\'e de Toulouse), Marie-H\'el\`ene Vignal (Universit\'e de Toulouse)
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a new numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system that is both asymptotically consistent and stable in the quasineutral regime, i.e. when the Debye length $\lambda$ is small compared to the characteristic spatial scale of the physical domain. Our approach consists in reformulating the Vlasov-Poisson system as a hyperbolic problem by applying a spectral expansion in the basis of Hermite functions in the velocity space and in designing a structure-preserving scheme for the time and spatial variables. Through this Hermite formulation, we establish a convergence result for the electric field toward its quasineutral limit together with explicit error estimates in $\lambda$. Following this path, we then propose a fully discrete numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system, inspired by the approach in arXiv:2306.14605, and rigorously prove that it is uniformly consistent in the quasineutral limit regime. Finally, we present several numerical simulations to illustrate the behavior of the proposed scheme. These results demonstrate the capability of our method to describe quasineutral plasmas, illustrate its stability and confirm its asymptotic preserving property.

papers.title: Phase diagram for intermittent maps
papers.abstract:
This paper studies the phase diagram of a fixed Pomeau--Manneville, or intermittent, map under a varying H\"older continuous potential of fixed exponent. Depending on the exponent, there are either one or two thermodynamic phases. The \emph{intermittent} phase is characterized by a unique Gibbs state whose typical orbits alternate irregularly between time intervals spent near the neutral fixed point and chaotic excursions away from it. The stationary phase is characterized by the Dirac mass at the neutral fixed point being the unique Gibbs state. Above a threshold exponent, every potential belongs to the intermittent phase, so the phase diagram is trivial. At or below the threshold, the phase transition locus is a co-dimension 1 topological submanifold separating the two phases, and it coincides with the set of potentials at which the pressure function fails to be real-analytic.
  This paper also investigates the relationships between the phase transition locus, (persistent) phase transitions in temperature, and ground states. It highlights a connection between phase transitions in temperature and ergodic optimization.

papers.title: Differentiable Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
papers.authors: Jonathan Frey, Katrin Baumg\"artner, Gianluca Frison, Dirk Reinhardt, Jasper Hoffmann, Leonard Fichtner, Sebastien Gros, Moritz Diehl
papers.abstract: The efficient computation of parametric solution sensitivities is a key challenge in the integration of learning-enhanced methods with nonlinear model predictive control, as their availability is crucial for many learning algorithms. This paper discusses the computation of solution sensitivities of general nonlinear programs using the implicit function theorem and smoothed optimality conditions treated in interior-point methods (IPM). We introduce sequential barrier quadratic programming (SBQP), which generalizes SQP with an IPM quadratic programming (QP) solver by allowing the barrier parameter to approach a prescribed nonnegative target value, recovering classical SQP when this target is zero. Previous works are limited to convex or unconstrained formulations, or lack an implementation for efficient sensitivity evaluation. The publication is accompanied by an efficient open-source implementation within the `acados` framework, providing both forward and adjoint sensitivities for general optimal control problems, achieving speedups exceeding 3x over the state-of-the-art solvers `mpc.pytorch` and `cvxpygen`.

papers.title: Smooth atlas stratified spaces, K-Homology Orientations, and Gysin maps, Part 1
papers.authors: Pierre Albin, Markus Banagl, Paolo Piazza
papers.abstract:
We introduce smooth atlas stratified spaces. We show that this class is closed under cartesian products; consequently, it is possible to define fiber bundles of smooth atlas stratified spaces. We describe the resolution of such a space to a manifold with fibered corners and use this result in order to prove that the class of smooth atlas stratified spaces coincides with that of Thom-Mather stratified spaces.
  We then consider Witt pseudomanifolds (such as singular complex algebraic varieties) where it is well-known that a bordism invariant signature is available and equal to the Fredholm index of a realization of the signature operator. To each oriented fiber bundle of stratified spaces, with Witt fibers, we assign a class in bivariant KK-theory (with 2 inverted). Kasparov multiplication by this element defines a Gysin map in analytic K-homology and one of our main results is that this Gysin map preserves the analytic signature class of Witt spaces. We prove in fact a more general result: functoriality for fiber bundles in the sense that if one fiber bundle is the composition of two others then the KK-class of the former is the Kasparov product of the classes of the latter. We also discuss this result for other Dirac-type operators satisfying an analytic Witt condition, for example the spin-Dirac operator on a fibration of psc-Witt spin pseudomanifolds. We next define the analytic Gysin map associated to an oriented normally non-singular inclusion of Witt spaces and prove that it also preserves the signature class.
  Finally, we relate the analytic signature class of a Witt space with the topological Siegel-Sullivan orientation. Specifically we show that if one applies the inverse of the second Adams operation to the Sullivan orientation and complexifies then one obtains our analytic signature class under the natural identification between analytic and topological K-homology.

papers.title: Optimal Sobolev embeddings for generalized Lorentz-Zygmund spaces
papers.abstract: This work deals with embeddings, of any integer order, for generalized Lorentz-Zygmund-Sobolev spaces on Euclidean domains satisfying minimal regularity assumptions. Explicit rearrangement-invariant, H\"older, Morrey and Campanato optimal target spaces are exhibited.

papers.title: Certified Monodromy Groups for Families of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: The monodromy group of a family of algebraic varieties is the group of isometries of the homology of a generic fibre, induced by parallel transport along a loop in the base space. We present a method to compute the monodromy group of families of generically smooth projective hypersurfaces using certified numerical algebraic geometry. This leads us to develop efficient algorithms for computing the discriminants of these families, which is of independent interest. Our flagship example is the case of families of symmetric cubic surfaces. The monodromy group is the Galois group of the 27 lines. We find that, when imposing symmetry, this Galois group is often a small subgroup of the Weyl group $W(E_6)$. We also include computational results for symmetric quartic surfaces.

papers.title: Three-Neighbour Bootstrap Percolation in Thin Three-Dimensional Grids
papers.abstract: We improve the status of the problem of determining minimum-sized percolating sets in $a \times b \times c$ grids under the $3$-neighbour process. Using several new constructions, we show that optimal percolating sets exist whenever $\min(a,b,c) \ge 7$. As an important step toward this, we also show that all grids with $\min(a,b,c) \ge 4$ have a percolating set whose size exactly achieves the lower bound $(ab+ac+bc)/3$ whenever this value is an integer.

papers.title: Decentralized Estimation and Control for Leader-Follower Networked Systems with Asymmetric Information Structure
papers.authors: Yiting Luo, Wei Wang, Qingyuan Qi
papers.abstract: In this paper, the decentralized estimation and linear quadratic (LQ) control problem for a leader-follower networked system (LFNS) is studied from the perspective of asymmetric information. Specifically, for a leader-follower network, the follower agent will be affected by the leader agent, while the follower agent will not affect the leader agent. Hence, the information sets accessed by the control variables of the leader agent and the follower agent are asymmetric, which will bring essential difficulties in finding the optimal control strategy. To this end, the orthogonal decomposition method is adopted to achieve the main results. The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows: Firstly, the optimal iterative estimation is derived using the conditional independence property established in this paper. Secondly, the optimal decentralized control strategy is derived by decoupling the forward-backward stochastic difference equations (FBSDEs), based on the derived optimal iterative estimation. Thirdly, the necessary and sufficient conditions for the feedback stabilization of the LFNS in infinite-horizon are derived. Finally, the proposed theoretical results are applied to solve the decentralized control problem of a leader-follower autonomous underwater vehicle (LF-AUV) system. The optimal control inputs for the AUVs are provided, and simulation results verify the effectiveness of the obtained results.

papers.title: Quasihomogeneous isolated singularities in terms of syzygies and foliations
papers.authors: Hamid Hassanzadeh, Abbas Nasrollah Nejad, Aron Simis
papers.abstract: One considers quasihomogeneous isolated singularities of hypersurfaces in arbitrary dimensions through the lenses of three apparently quite apart themes: syzygies, singularity invariants, and foliations. In the first of these, one adds to the well-known result of Saito a syzygy-theoretic characterization of a quasihomogeneous singularity affording an effective computational criterion. In the second theme, one explores the Milnor-Tjurina difference number from a commutative algebra viewpoint. Building on the Briancon-Skoda theorem and exponent, we extend previously known inequalities by Dimca and Greuel to arbitrary dimension and provide algebraic formulas involving the syzygy-theoretic part and reduction exponents. In the last theme, one recovers and brings to algebraic light a result of Camacho and Movasati by establishing a couple of characterizations of quasihomogeneous isolated singularities in terms of the generators of the module of invariant vector fields.

papers.title: Stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics and its zero-mass limit
papers.abstract: We introduce a stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics with positive mass and study its zero--mass limit. The new aspect of this paper is that we only fix the initial and terminal probability distributions of the positions of particles under consideration, but not those of their velocities, with Heisenberg's uncertainty principle in mind. In the zero--mass limit, we show that the minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is tight if and only if the initial momentum (=(mass)$\times$(velocity)) of a particle converges to zero. We also prove that the limit of minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is a minimizer of a standard stochastic optimal transport for continuous semimartingales.

papers.title: Free energy Wasserstein gradient flow and their particle counterparts: toy model, (degenerate) PL inequalities and exit times
papers.abstract:
In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process.
  The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points.
  In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general {\L}ojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.

papers.title: An Expander Mixing Lemma for Directed Graphs via Transition Matrices
papers.abstract: We establish an Expander Mixing Lemma for directed graphs in terms of the eigenvalues of a transition matrix, extending the classical spectral inequality to the non-symmetric setting. This formulation works with the complex spectrum of the transition matrix and incorporates the conditioning of its eigenbasis through a condition number. For connected, non-bipartite, undirected regular graphs, the result reduces to the classical Expander Mixing Lemma. More generally, the theorem provides a framework for studying structural properties of directed graphs through the spectra of non-normal matrices.

papers.title: Semibricks and wide subcategories in extended module categories
papers.abstract: For $d\geq 1$, we define semibricks and wide subcategories in the $d$-extended hearts of bounded $t$-structures on a triangulated category. We show that these semibricks are in bijection with finite-length wide subcategories. When the $d$-extended heart is the $d$-extended module category $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}\Lambda$ of a finite-dimensional algebra $\Lambda$ over a field, we define left/right-finite semibricks and left/right-finite wide subcategories in $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}\Lambda$ and show bijections with $(d+1)$-term simple-minded collections, generalising the bijections between $2$-term simple-minded collections, left/right-finite wide subcategories and left/right-finite semibricks in $\mathrm{mod}\Lambda$. We use a relation between semibricks and silting complexes to characterise which mutations of $(d+1)$-term silting complexes are again $(d+1)$-term.

papers.title: A Two-Term Ziv-Zakai Bound for Multitarget DoA Estimation in MIMO Radar
papers.authors: Mohammadreza Bakhshizadeh Mohajer, Daniela Tuninetti, Luca Barletta
papers.abstract: Multitarget direction of arrival (DoA) estimation is challenging when fluctuating targets are closely spaced: local Cram\'er--Rao bounds (CRBs) miss global errors, while direct vector Ziv--Zakai bound (ZZB) evaluation is computationally demanding. For colocated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with Swerling-II fluctuations and an ordered angular prior, we derive a rigorous two-term Bayesian mean squared error lower bound. A finite separation contribution addresses nonlocal discrimination, while a correction based on the prior averaged Fisher information matrix (FIM) retains target coupling and virtual array geometry. We show that the prior averaged pointwise CRB diverges under unrestricted target spacing when the FIM is nonsingular almost everywhere, although the proposed bound remains finite. Once the averaged FIM is obtained, evaluation avoids displacement optimization and multidimensional binary error integration. The bound supports analysis of snapshot diversity, target spacing, and transmit and receive allocation. Numerical comparison with the vector ZZB shows close agreement at low SNR but greater conservatism at high SNR, quantifying the tradeoff in tightness.

papers.title: Phase transition for conditional covariance matrices estimated by importance sampling, and implications for cross-entropy schemes in high dimension
papers.authors: Jason Beh, Jerome Morio, Florian Simatos
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent high-dimensional reliability algorithms, we study a random matrix model corresponding to the estimation by importance sampling of $\Sigma_A$, the covariance matrix of a Gaussian vector conditioned by a rare event $A$. For such models, we show that, in contrast to most random matrix models, the minimal sample size to ensure an accurate estimation of $\Sigma_A$ needs to grow superlinearly in the dimension. More precisely, if $n$ is the sample size and $d$ the dimension, we show that the estimation of $\Sigma_A$ is accurate if $n/d \gg L$ and not accurate if $n/d \ll L$ where $L$ is the maximum likelihood ratio. Moreover, we relate the asymptotic behavior of $L$ to $\lambda_1$, the smallest eigenvalue of the auxiliary covariance matrix, which suggests that $L$ (and thus the minimal sample size) will be larger for small values of $\lambda_1$. Numerical experiments confirm that this insight carries over to recent cross-entropy algorithms, with the best performing algorithms being also the ones with the largest smallest eigenvalue. Although backed up by our theoretical result, this result is surprising as these algorithms were not designed to act on the spectrum.

papers.title: Exponential Decays of Steklov Eigenfunctions for the Magnetic Laplacian
papers.abstract: Consider the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\beta$ associated with the Schr\"odinger operator $(D+\beta \A)^2$ with a magnetic potential in a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$, where $\beta>1$ is the field strength parameter. Assume that the magnetic field $\B=\nabla \times \A$ is of finite type. We show that if $\beta>\beta_0$, the ground state for $\Lambda_\beta$ decays exponentially away from a neighborhood of the subset of $\partial\Omega$, on which $\B$ vanishes to the maximal order.

papers.title: Sharp Convergence to the Half-Space for Mullins-Sekerka in the Plane
papers.authors: Wenhui Shi, Maria G. Westdickenberg, Michael Westdickenberg
papers.abstract: We revisit the HED Method for the Mullins-Sekerka evolution in the plane. We identify a natural notion of distance, intrinsic to the interface itself. Using this distance, the energy, and the dissipation, we develop natural assumptions on the flow and, assuming existence of a solution satisfying these conditions, obtain not just the algebraic rate (already previously derived by Chugreeva, Otto, and M.G. Westdickenberg) but also the sharp leading order constant for the convergence to the flat limiting interface. To carry this out, we introduce a lemma that obtains optimal algebraic decay behavior (rate and prefactor) from given variational information.

papers.title: Regularity for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption
papers.authors: Jiangwen Wang, Jo\~ao Vitor da Silva, Feida Jiang

papers.title: Absolute incidence theorems and tilings
papers.abstract: We give a precise definition of incidence theorems in plane projective geometry and introduce the notion of absolute incidence theorems, which hold over any ring. Fomin and Pylyavskyy describe how to obtain incidence theorems from tilings of an orientable surface; they call this result the master theorem. Instances of the master theorem are always absolute incidence theorems. As most classically known incidence theorems are instances of the master theorem, they are absolute incidence theorems. We give an explicit example of an incidence theorem involving 13 points that is not an absolute incidence theorem, and therefore is not an instance of the master theorem.

papers.title: Cyclic sieving phenomena for trees and tree-rooted maps
papers.abstract: We prove cyclic sieving phenomena satisfied by corner-rooted plane trees (alias ordered trees). The sets of rooted plane trees that we consider are: (1) all trees with $n$ nodes; (2) all trees with $n$ nodes and $k$ leaves; (3) all trees with a given degree distribution of the nodes. Moreover, we consider four different cyclic group actions: (1) the root is moved to the next corner along a tour of the tree; (2) only trees in which the root is at a leaf are considered, and the action moves the root to the next leaf; (3) only trees in which the root is at a non-leaf are considered, and the action moves the root to the next non-leaf corner; (4) only trees in which the root is at a node of degree $\delta$ are considered, for a fixed $\delta$, and the action moves the root to the next corner of this type. We prove a cyclic sieving phenomenon for each meaningful combination of these sets and actions. As a bonus, we also establish corresponding cyclic sieving phenomena for tree-rooted planar maps.

papers.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
papers.authors: Wooyeon Kim, Jens Marklof, Matthew Welsh
papers.abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain's proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is for example $1,2^{1/3},2^{-1/3}$. This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature $(2,2)$. The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature $(3,3)$ in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})^3\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^3$ over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner's measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

papers.title: The complexity of being monitorable
papers.abstract: We study monitorable sets from a topological standpoint. In particular, we use descriptive set theory to describe the complexity of the family of monitorable sets in a countable space $X$. When $X$ is second countable, we observe that the family of monitorable sets is $\Pi^0_3$ and determine the exact complexities it can have. In contrast, we show that if $X$ is not second countable then the family of monitorable sets can be much more complex, giving an example where it is $ \Pi^1_1$-complete.

papers.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
papers.abstract: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-\delta})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $\delta>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.

papers.title: The symmetrized sum of finite $q$-multiple harmonic sums with one exceptional index
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give explicit expressions for $q$-harmonic sums on $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ indices. The case $A=1$ has been extensively studied, and a variety of identities, explicit evaluations, and structural properties are known. Likewise, numerous explicit evaluations are available for $q$-multiple zeta values and $q$-harmonic sums with uniform indices $A-\cdots-A$. Although several methods are available for treating non-uniform indices, explicit evaluations for the pattern $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ remain comparatively scarce. The case $A=2$ was settled only recently. In this paper, we extend this framework to the general case $A\ge3$ as the total sum with the theory of the elementary symmetric functions, though we do not generally evaluate each summand at a prescribed position of $A$. We obtain explicit formulas in terms of binomial coefficients and degenerate Bernoulli numbers. Some expressions about $2-\cdots-2,A,2-\cdots-2$ are also shown.

papers.title: A family of matrix flows converging to normal matrices
papers.abstract: The celebrated Antezana-Pujals-Stojanoff Theorem states that the iterated Aluthge transforms of an arbitrary matrix converge to a normal matrix. We introduce a family of matrix flows that share this convergence property by defining them through ordinary differential equations. The family includes a continuous analogue of the Aluthge transform, as well as a differential equation discussed by Haagerup in the context of II$_1$ factors. We also examine the same type of flows in the setting of Hilbert space operators equipped with unitarily invariant norms.

papers.title: Revisiting the Algebraic and Analytic Descriptions of Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: The Wintner-Wielandt theorem exposes a fundamental incompatibility between the canonical commutation relation (CCR) and the Hilbert-space formulation of quantum mechanics. While the conventional approach preserves the CCR by extending the Hilbert-space framework to a rigged Hilbert space, this work develops the complementary alternative. Retaining the Hilbert space, the unavoidable trace obstruction requires a boundary modification of the CCR, consistently realizable only in a space of finite, albeit arbitrarily large, dimension. In this setting, the eigenvalue problems of position and momentum admit explicit solutions within the Hilbert space. We show that the highest-energy components of the position eigenvectors retain a non-vanishing uniform weight, implying that the full spectrum remains relevant. The resulting autonomous matrix algebra also yields a new physical observable, the action difference. In the position basis, this observable gives rise to a momentum matrix with a discrete Cauchy kernel. After an alternating phase transformation, this matrix acts on plane waves in the infinite equidistant lattice model as the Schroedinger momentum operator, revealing a structural connection between the algebraic and analytic approaches. This framework retains the standard Hilbert-space spectral theory and remains closely connected to the familiar analytical structure of quantum mechanics, including the momentum operator and the uncertainty principle.

papers.title: Novel technique based on L\'eja Points Approximation for Log-determinant Estimation of Large matrices
papers.authors: Verlon Roel Mbingui, Antoine Tambue, Issa Karambal
papers.abstract:
The computation of the Log-determinant of large, sparse, symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices is essential in many scientific computational fields such as numerical linear algebra and machine learning. In low dimensions, Cholesky is preferred, but in high dimensions, its computation may be prohibitive due to memory limitation. To circumvent this, Krylov subspace techniques have proven to be efficient but may be computationally expensive due to the required orthogonalization processes. In this paper, we introduce a Newton-L\'eja interpolation based approach for estimating log-determinants, where the implementation is only based on matrix multiplications and a rough estimation of eigenvalue bounds of the matrix. The method employs an adaptive stopping criterion to select the degree of interpolation according to the data and introduces a centered, scaled-based formulation for computing the logarithmic divided differences. By combining Newton-L\'eja interpolation with a randomized algorithm called Hutch++, we obtain a matrix-free log-determinant estimation framework that avoids explicit matrix factorization and Krylov basis orthogonalization. We establish approximation error bounds for the Newton-L\'eja interpolation and derive an inexact oracle error bound that separates stochastic trace estimation from the approximation errors in the projected and residual components.
  Numerical experiments on both large sparse synthetic matrices (Gaussian Markov Random fields) and large-scale real-world matrices demonstrate that our method substantially reduces computational time while retaining competitive accuracy, thereby confirming its effectiveness, scalability, and favorable accuracy-cost trade-off for large-scale log-determinant estimation compared with stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ) and related stochastic trace-estimation methods.

papers.title: Topological insights into Monoids and Module systems
papers.abstract:
Let $H$ be a monoid and let $G$ denote its quotient groupoid. We introduce the Riemann-Zariski space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ associated with $H$ and prove that it is a spectral space. We then show that, if $H$ is an $s$-Pr\"ufer monoid, the space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ is homeomorphic to the prime $s$-spectrum of $H$ endowed with the Zariski topology.
  Next, given a finitary ideal system $r$ on $H$, we prove that the space of $r$-ideals $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$, endowed with the Zariski topology, is spectral, and that the prime $r$-spectrum of $H$ is proconstructible in $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$.
  We also introduce a new topology on the set $\mathcal{X}$ of all generalized $H$-module systems and study its properties. In particular, we show that $\mathcal{X}$ and its subspace $\mathcal{X}_{\textup{fin}}$ of finitary generalized $H$-module systems are spectral spaces.
  Finally, we provide a characterization of those subsets of the set of overmonoids of $H$ that are quasi-compact.

papers.title: A Novel Two-Parameter Penalty: Relaxation Degree Analysis and Sparse Signal Recovery
papers.authors: Ziwei Li, Wengu Chen, Huanmin Ge, Dachun Yang
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce a nonconvex two-parameter penalty function $P_{a,p}$, parameterized by $a\in(0,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1]$, and the relaxation degree RD$_P$ for a separable nonconvex penalty function $P$. Based on $P_{a,p}$, we further propose the $P_{a,p}$ minimization framework for sparse signal recovery. This framework generalizes the TL1 minimization model established by S. Zhang and J. Xin (corresponding to the special case $p=1$) and provides a unified family of nonconvex penalty functions for sparse signal recovery. Using the sparse convex-combination technique, we establish both exact and stable sparse signal recovery under the restricted isometry property (RIP). To efficiently solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we apply a modified iteratively re-weighted least squares method and the difference of convex functions algorithm (DCA) to develop the IRLSTLp algorithm for unconstrained $P_{a,p}$ minimization and prove some convergence results. Finally, numerical experiments compare recovery and runtime against single- and double-loop baselines, examine sensitivity to $(a,p)$, and assess the empirical correlation between RD$_{P_{a,p}}$ and recovery within the proposed family.

papers.title: Regularity of the Value Function in Discounted Infinite-Time Mean Field Games
papers.abstract: In [18], we introduced discounted infinite-time mean field games. Subsequently, in [19], we studied the connection between infinite-time mean field FBSDEs and elliptic master equations. In this paper, we further investigate the regularity of the representative player's value function $V(x,\mu)$. We first establish strong well-posedness and uniqueness in law for an extended class of infinite-time FBSDEs. In the weighted $L_r^2$ framework, we construct directional variations and obtain a bounded continuous representation of the Lions-derivative of $\partial_xV$. Under additional smoothness and quantitative stability assumptions, $L_r^p$ estimates for scalar linear FBSDEs allow us to establish the existence of higher-order derivatives of $\partial_xV$. Consequently, $\partial_xV$ is a classical solution of the elliptic master equation for the value function's derivative.

papers.title: Biregular bipartite multigraphs and matchings in tensor products of bipartite graphs
papers.authors: Ilya I. Bogdanov, Fedor Petrov, Anton Sadovnichiy, Fedor Ushakov
papers.abstract: We answer a question of P. Higgins on permutations and involutions in binary arrays, arising in the study of regular finite semigroups. For a binary rectangular matrix M, we prove that if there is a permutation pi(x, y) = (f(x, y), g(x, y)) of its cells satisfying M(x, g(x,y)) = 1 for every cell, then there is an involution with the same property. The elementary proof places coins in the nonzero cells, reduces their support to a forest, and assigns consecutive integer weights to the coins incident to each row and column. We also prove a multiplicativity formula for bipartite expansion and a perfect matching theorem for tensor products of supports of matrices with prescribed margins. We study a stronger conjecture of F. Petrov on disjoint swaps in biregular bipartite multigraphs. We prove this conjecture for k = mn + eps, |eps| <= 2, and for n = 6, k = 6m + 3, and give a group-theoretic reformulation.

papers.title: Discrete hypocoercive estimates for discontinuous Galerkin methods: application to the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system
papers.authors: Yi Cai (USTC), Alain Blaustein (RAPSODI), Tao Xiong (USTC), Francis Filbet (IMT)
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a class of structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin schemes for the nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck model, reformulated as a hyperbolic system through a Hermite expansion in the velocity variable. We discretize the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation with the discontinuous Galerkin method, while the Poisson equation is approximated with either a discontinuous Galerkin method or a Raviart-Thomas mixed finite element method. We prove the exponential relaxation to equilibrium for suitable initial data, uniformly with respect to the discretization parameters thanks to discrete hypocoercivity arguments. Moreover, we check that the resulting semi-discrete schemes preserve the physical invariants along with the L 2 variational structure of the linearized model. Numerical simulations verify the accuracy and the long-time behavior of the scheme.

papers.title: Inversion monotonicity in subclasses of the 1324-avoiders
papers.authors: Anders Claesson, Svante Linusson, Henning Ulfarsson, Emil Verkama
papers.abstract: We prove injectively that the pattern-avoiding permutation classes $\mathrm{Av}(1324, 231)$ and $\mathrm{Av}(1324, 2314, 3214, 4213)$ are inversion monotone: for every $k$, the number of length-$n$ permutations with $k$ inversions in either class is weakly increasing in $n$. These are the first known nontrivial examples of the phenomenon. The latter is a special case of a general construction. We also characterize the finitely based permutation classes in which the number of length-$n$ members with a fixed number of inversions stabilizes as $n$ grows, and determine the limiting values for all classes $\mathrm{Av}(1324, p)$ with $p \in S_4$. Connections to several nice families of integer partitions are revealed. Lastly, we show that for asymptotically almost every pattern $p \in \mathrm{Av}(1324)$, the class $\mathrm{Av}(1324, p)$ is inversion monotone in the region $n \geq \frac{k+7}{2}$, expanding on the work of Linusson and Verkama. This work is motivated by the conjectures of Claesson, Jel\'inek and Steingr\'imsson that $\mathrm{Av}(1324)$, and more generally $\mathrm{Av}(p)$ for every nonidentity pattern $p$, is inversion monotone.

papers.title: A Note on the Resolvent Algebra and Functional Integral Approach to the Free Bose Einstein Condensation
papers.abstract: Quasiparticles whose number is not conserved are generally considered not to condense in equilibrium, although a Bose--Einstein condensation can formally appear in particle--Bose field interacting systems. As a basis for examining this mathematically, we formulate the condensation of the free Bose gas with resolvent algebras and probability theory: above the critical density, the condensate state is a standard complex Gaussian mixture of disjoint factor states, which is its central decomposition and corresponds to the ergodic decomposition of a Gaussian measure for the real-time evolution.

papers.title: Exotic Hopf maps, weight shifting and applications to vector bundles
papers.abstract: Using motivic homotopy theory we produce several explicit polynomial representatives of the suspension of the Hopf map defined over the integers. We derive from this computation an explicit rank 2 vector bundle on the Jouanolou device of the projective space of dimension 3 over the integers.

papers.title: DeepRitzSplit: A Variational Neural Operator Framework for Gradient Flows with Application to Dendritic Growth
papers.authors: Beno\^it Appolaire, Ludovick Gagnon, Chih-Kang Huang, Miha Zalo\v{z}nik
papers.abstract:
Phase-field models are widely used to simulate microstructure evolution but their numerical solution remains computationally demanding. Neural operator surrogates provide a promising alternative, yet existing approaches are data-driven, requiring large datasets and exhibiting limited robustness when extrapolating to unseen configurations.
  We introduce DeepRitzSplit, an unsupervised neural operator framework for gradient-flow systems based on a variational formulation of energy-stable splitting schemes. It learns the time evolution semigroup associated with a convex-concave free-energy decomposition by minimizing the underlying variational problem at each time step. It is designed to inherit the dissipative structure of the underlying gradient flow without requiring trajectory datasets.
  We further introduce a Reaction-Diffusion Neural Operator (RDNO) architecture motivated by splitting schemes, with separate reaction and diffusion components to improve training efficiency and interpretability.
  We assess the approach on the Allen-Cahn equation and apply it to a phase-field model of anisotropic dendritic growth during solidification. In the Allen-Cahn benchmark, DeepRitzSplit shows better generalization than the supervised baseline on the out-of-distribution configurations tested, using 180 training configurations. In dendritic growth, the method captures the overall phase morphology and dendrite tip velocity well, while the tip radius is more sensitive to the training strategy. Refinement based on the residual of the splitting scheme markedly improves this second-order morphological quantity. The trained operators retain good predictive capabilities on configurations substantially different from the training set.
  These results demonstrate the potential of variationally trained neural operators as physically informed surrogates for accelerated microstructure simulations.

papers.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
papers.abstract: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

papers.title: Adaptive refinement based on local approximation power of hierarchical spline spaces
papers.authors: Gustavo A. Fernandez Lezcano, Eduardo M. Garau, B\'arbara S. Ivaniszyn
papers.abstract: We propose an adaptive refinement strategy for hierarchical B-splines that increases the approximation power of every marked cell by at least one. Here, the approximation power of a cell is the finest level $\ell$ such that all the B-splines of level $\ell$ that do not vanish on the cell belong to the hierarchical space. This increase can be achieved with the standard refinement of hierarchical meshes, in which each cell is subdivided at most once per step, provided that the regions formed at each level by the cells with this property are nested. We call the hierarchical meshes with this nesting property \emph{weakly admissible}, characterize them, and prove that the proposed refinement preserves weak admissibility. We also prove a complexity estimate: the number of cells created along the adaptive process is bounded by a constant times the total number of marked cells. Moreover, we extend known local $L^q$ estimates for a multilevel quasi-interpolant on these meshes to Sobolev norms, showing that the local error bound on each active cell is governed by its approximation power, which supports using this quantity to drive the refinement. Numerical experiments illustrate the local gain of resolution produced by the proposed strategy, as well as its robustness with respect to the marking criterion and the marking parameter.

papers.title: A structure-preserving semi-implicit finite volume scheme on vertex-staggered unstructured meshes
papers.authors: Elena Bernardelli, Elena Gaburro, Michael Dumbser
papers.abstract: We present a structure-preserving semi-implicit finite volume method on vertex-based staggered meshes for the compatible discretization of first-order systems of time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs). The method preserves divergence-free and curl-free vector fields exactly thanks to the compatible vertex-staggered discretization of the state variables on unstructured grids consisting of primal Delaunay triangles and their dual polygons. For the weakly compressible Euler equations, the scheme is asymptotic preserving, yielding a consistent discretization of the incompressible limit as the Mach number goes to zero. The scheme applies to a broad spectrum of PDEs, including the weakly compressible and incompressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system, and the incompressible version of the first-order hyperbolic Godunov-Peshkov-Romenski (GPR) model for continuum mechanics. The computational domain is covered by a primal triangular mesh and a dual tessellation made of star polygons. Scalar quantities (pressure, density, viscous stress) are defined at nodes, with pressure updated implicitly in a continuous finite element fashion, yielding a symmetric and positive definite pressure system. Instead, vector fields (velocity, momentum, magnetic and distortion fields) are stored at triangle barycenters and evolved explicitly using a compatible finite volume scheme. With the semi-implicit discretization, the CFL restriction is independent of the sound speed, allowing simulations at low Mach numbers. The compatible formulation ensures an exactly divergence-free velocity field in the incompressible limit, an exactly divergence-free magnetic field for MHD, and an exactly curl-free inverse deformation gradient in solid mechanics. The scheme has been extended to second-order accuracy. The method is validated through a set of test cases.

papers.title: A generalisation of the Gagliardo--Nirenberg Inequality with applications to mass-critical and mass-subcritical elliptic equations
papers.abstract: Via a new inequality \`a la Gagliardo--Nirenberg, we prove the existence and nonexistence of solutions to \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} (-\Delta)^s u + \frac{\mu}{|y|^{2s}} u + \lambda u = f(u), \quad \mathbb{R}^N \ni x = (y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^K \times \mathbb{R}^{N-K}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} u^2 \, \mathrm{d}x = \rho \end{cases} \end{equation*} in the mass-critical and mass-subcritical regimes, where $s>0$, $N \ge K \ge 2$, $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ belongs to a specific range, $\rho>0$ is given a priori, and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ is unknown. Additionally, we obtain similar results for the problem above with $\mu=0$ and $N \ge 1$ as well as a related curl-curl equation. Finally, we provide a thorough insight into the threshold for $\rho$ that divides the scenarios of negative and zero least energy.

papers.title: A High Dimensional Wild Bootstrap Max-Test for Detecting the Presence of Significant Predictors
papers.abstract: We construct a block bootstrap max-test for detecting the presence of significant predictors in a high dimensional setting, allowing for weakly dependent and heterogeneous (possibly non-stationary) data. The number of covariates to be screened may be large $p$ $>>$ $n$, and growing at an exponential rate, provided $\ln (p)$ $=$ $o(n^{a})$ for some $a$ $>$ $0$ that depends on memory decay and the growth of higher moments. We study the problem of correlation screening in a high dimensional marginal regression setting, assuming so-called \textit{physical dependence} in a time series setting. We entirely sidestep covariance matrix estimation and adaptive re-sampling by working with a max-statistic over the many computed parameters. Thus we do not need endogenous selection of the most relevant predictor index yielding non-uniform asymptotics, nor do we need a post-estimation Bonferroni correction. The sequence of non-standard approximating distributions arising from the maximum of an increasing number of estimators is easily approximated by a multiplier (wild) block bootstrap. The max-test controls for size well, performs well against various deviations from the null, including very slight deviations with a weak or sparse signal. A numerical experiment is performed and an empirical example with the VIX volatility index is provided.

papers.title: Data-Driven Continuous-Time LQR: Linking Reinforcement Learning and Behavioral System Theory
papers.authors: Armin Gie{\ss}ler, Felix Th\"ommes, S\"oren Hohmann
papers.abstract: Behavioral system theory and reinforcement learning (RL) have independently developed data-driven approaches to the continuous-time LQR problem, yet their respective methods have largely evolved in separation. We connect these two adjacent lines of work by studying their data-driven parameterizations, namely a closed-loop (CL) parameterization from behavioral system theory and an integral RL (IRL) parameterization. The CL parameterization characterizes the closed-loop system via a matrix that satisfies equality constraints. While this parameterization has been extensively studied for discrete-time systems, we adapt key results to the continuous-time setting and develop a policy iteration (PI) scheme, derive an algebraic Riccati equation, and introduce an alternative convex program. The IRL parameterization utilizes off-policy data to perform policy evaluation, which is used for PI or value iteration. Within the IRL framework, we derive a policy gradient flow and propose convex programs for the LQR problem. Finally, we provide a unified treatment of these parameterizations that enables a systematic understanding of existing approaches, and clarifies their structural relationships.

papers.title: A Measure-Theoretic Formulation of Behavioral Systems
papers.abstract: Ensemble control specifies probability laws on admissible trajectories, including their temporal dependence. Starting from an arbitrary closed behavior, we organize its laws into a framework that connects standard probability-measure geometry, occupation-measure control, and data-driven trajectory parametrization. Classical convexity and extreme-point properties describe the feasible laws, while classical Bellman duality governs additive control objectives. On compact state and input spaces, full-path constrained duality for continuous trajectory functions gives primal attainment and zero gap whenever feasible. For controllable linear time-invariant systems, the noise-free Fundamental Lemma yields an equivalent law-level Hankel factorization, with a canonical pseudoinverse lift. The factorization transfers trajectory-law constraints exactly to coefficient space and connects them to covariance control. Explicit noisy-Hankel bounds quantify subspace approximation for second-moment-bounded laws under known rank and Gaussian output measurement noise. Numerical studies include a nonlinear reset problem whose nonadjacent correlation constraint requires temporal memory, covariance-constrained optimization, and noisy-data policy evaluation. Known transition kernels provide a further structural perspective through history-conditional consistency.

papers.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on Cayley graphs over dihedral groups
papers.authors: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya, Xiwang Cao
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of Cayley graphs over dihedral groups that exhibit perfect state transfer between distinct vertex states in Grover walks. For $n\ge 3$, let $D_n:=\langle a,b : a^n=b^2=1,\ bab=a^{-1}\rangle$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$, and let $S\subseteq D_n\setminus\{1\}$ satisfying $S=S^{-1}$ and $\langle S\rangle =D_n$. We show that the Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(D_n,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $(D_n,S)$ is equivalent to one of the following pairs: $(D_n,\{b,ba\})$; $(D_n,\{a,a^{-1},ba,ba^{-1}\})$, where $4$ does not divide $n$; or $(D_{2m},\{b,ba^{m},ba,ba^{m+1}\})$, where $m$ is odd. Our proof combines the representation theory of $D_n$ with tools from algebraic number theory.

papers.title: Self-Distillation is Optimal Among Spectral Shrinkage Estimators
papers.authors: Radu Lecoiu, Debarghya Mukherjee, Pragya Sur
papers.abstract: Self-distillation has emerged as a promising technique for improving model performance in modern machine learning systems. We develop the statistical foundations of self-distillation in high-dimensional linear regression by introducing and analyzing a broad class of estimators, namely spectral shrinkage estimators. We consider both spiked and general covariance matrices. For the former, we establish that when the covariance has $s$ distinct spikes, $s$-step self-distillation achieves optimal prediction among spectral shrinkage estimators, outperforming well-known estimators in statistics and machine learning. Moreover, we show that $s$ steps are necessary for optimality: any $(s-k)$-step distilled estimator is strictly suboptimal for $1 \leq k \leq s$. For general covariance matrices, we show that self-distillation approaches the optimal limiting prediction risk among continuous spectral shrinkage estimators as the number of distillation steps increases. We further develop a generalized cross-validation procedure for selecting the distillation parameters from data and establish an asymptotic oracle guarantee for the resulting estimator. We also study a federated approach where multiple data centers share spectral shrinkage estimators and a common server seeks to aggregate them to achieve optimal performance.
