In this case, we find that the best local rule again takes the form of self-distillation, though it differs from the optimal rule when data are hosted centrally on a single server. Together, our results explain why self-distillation improves predictive performance and provide a broader statistical framework that connects it to classical shrinkage-based methods.

papers.title: Implementation-Based Incentive Design for Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand and Transit Systems
papers.authors: Xinling Li, Runyu Zhang, Gioele Zardini
papers.abstract: Achieving a socially desirable operating point for a multimodal transportation system is challenging when Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand (AMoD) and Public Transit (PT) operators pursue selfish objectives alongside endogenous passenger choices. Existing equilibrium-based regulation models typically search over municipal policies to predict the induced operator equilibrium, creating strong behavioral assumptions, equilibrium-selection issues, and difficult bilevel optimization problems. This paper proposes an implementation-based alternative. Rather than asking which municipal action induces the best equilibrium, we ask: given a target operating profile, what minimum realized transfer makes unilateral deviation unattractive for each operator? Using k-implementation theory, this payment decomposes into two unilateral deviation gains: one for the AMoD operator and one for PT. Calculating this payment requires computing three distinct objects: the social target, the AMoD best response, and the PT best response. This is nontrivial because each represents a large-scale network optimization problem complicated by endogenous mode choice and congestion. To address this, we develop tailored mathematical formulations and algorithms for each oracle. For the social target, we derive a decomposition and entropy-regularized mixed-integer convex formulation balancing social optimality and implementability. For the AMoD oracle, we derive an exact reformulation, a convex relaxation providing a global upper bound, and a sequential convex approximation for feasible lower bounds. For the PT oracle, we develop a mixed-integer convex relaxation and characterize its exactness condition. A NYC case study shows the framework computes tight implementation-payment bounds and reveals how the dominant source of incentive misalignment shifts with congestion.

papers.title: Generalized Fermat equation over cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_l$-extensions of totally real fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a totally real field of odd degree $m$ in which $2$ is inert. Let $l\geq5$ be a prime totally ramified in $K$ with $\gcd(m,l(l-1)/2)=1$ and $2^{l-1}\not\equiv1\pmod{l^2}$. We prove the asymptotic Fermat's Last Theorem over every layer $K_{n,l}$, $n\geq1$, of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_l$-extension of $K$. Using $S$-unit bounds, we also give criteria for the generalized Fermat equation $Ax^p+By^p=Cz^p$ to have no asymptotic solutions in $K_{n,l}^3$ when the coefficients $A,B,C$ are supported at the primes above $2$ or $2d$, with $d$ an odd prime. In particular, for every fixed integer $r\geq2$ other than $4$, the equation $x^p+y^p=2^rz^p$ has no asymptotic solutions in $K_{n,l}^3$ for each fixed $n\geq1$. Thorne's modularity theorem makes the resulting bounds effective in each layer $\mathbb{Q}_{n,l}$ to which our criteria apply.

papers.title: Robust Ensemble Kalman Filtering Under Observation Noise Misspecification
papers.abstract: We address observation noise misspecification in Bayesian filtering of dynamical systems via generalised Bayesian inference. Mismatch in tail decay between the true data generating process and an assumed observation model, often indicated via outliers, can strongly impact Bayesian updates in Kalman filters and their ensemble approximations. Adjusting information processing in the analysis step by employing diffusion score matching achieves robustness while maintaining closed-form Gaussian updates and good uncertainty quantification. We provide theoretical properties of this novel Kalman filter in linear Gaussian state space systems covering conjugacy of the analysis step, robustness, covariance stability, and tuning. We extend the approach to non-linear signal dynamics by adapting ensemble Kalman filter variants. Simulation studies on 2D target tracking and the Lorenz-63 and 40D Lorenz-96 systems highlight a critical trade-off between robustness and stability in filtering.

papers.title: The Bogomolov property for $p$-supercuspidal eigenforms
papers.authors: Andrea Conti, Pietro Piras, Lea Terracini
papers.abstract: We prove a lower bound on the Weil height, the so-called Bogomolov property, for the algebraic extensions of $\mathbb Q$ cut out by the adelic Galois representations attached to certain eigenforms whose local component at a prime $p$ is supercuspidal. To this end, we give a method for constructing metric inequalities over $p$-adic Lie extensions of fields over $\mathbb Q$ that are finitely ramified at $p$.

papers.title: Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths
papers.abstract: We study finite expected-signature information for mixed-fBm paths with Hurst indices above $1/4$. Up to level three, the only parameter-dependent expected features are the variance transform $q_\theta$ and the time-ordered transform $R_\theta$. We prove the scale tradeoff $2K$ level-two scales versus $K$ selected level-two/three scales, together with separation and local inverse bounds.

papers.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
papers.authors: Ragnar Freij-Hollanti, Kirsten D. Morris, Patricija \v{S}apokait\.e
papers.abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.

papers.title: Closed-form fractional radial links for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis
papers.abstract: We study binary classification when the two classes are elliptical with a shared radial generator $g$. The log-likelihood ratio is then an additive function of the two squared Mahalanobis radii, with radial link $\varphi=\log g$. For Gaussian classes $\varphi$ is affine and the rule reduces to quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA); otherwise the Bayes link is not the identity. Instead of fitting this link with a spline smoother, we derive its family from the within-class law of the radius and estimate a finite fractional-power projection. We prove that the link is identifiable from the radius law, that the plug-in estimator is $\sqrt{n}$-consistent and asymptotically normal under finite-moment conditions, and that the induced classifier is asymptotically Bayes-optimal in an iterated sieve limit. For $d\ge2$ and non-nested class parameters, the identity link suffices only for affine (Gaussian) generators. The bridge, GAM membership and the affine direction of this dichotomy are verified in Lean 4. We compare against the global Mahalanobis-GAM of Ghosh et al. (2025), re-implemented with mgcv REML splines at equal input budget. On two UCI benchmarks the derived link ties with the fitted GAM. On six financial series from three asset classes, with validation that respects temporal dependence, it is never significantly worse than the fitted GAM: better on CAD/USD and tied on the other five. It beats QDA on the three heaviest-tailed series (oil $[+0.023,+0.069]$, S&P 500 $[+0.039,+0.125]$, JPY/USD $[+0.009,+0.047]$) and ties elsewhere. A rate simulation with a closed-form ground truth reproduces the $\sqrt{n}$ rate and, under covariance heterogeneity, QDA's risk floor against the derived link's vanishing excess risk. The derived link thus matches a tuned GAM without smoothing-parameter selection and improves on QDA where the generator departs from the Gaussian.

papers.title: Transformation theorem and monotonicity of the numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls
papers.abstract:
In \cite{HH}, H. Huang-X.Huang introduced the generalized Reifenberg condition which describes the non-increasing property of numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls and gave a transformation theorem under this condition. In this note, we study how almost Euclidean factors of concentric geodesic balls interact with harmonic splitting maps under a lower Ricci curvature bound and prove a dimension gap for harmonic functions of almost linear growth and then derive a transformation theorem under a non-decreasing property compared with the non-increasing property above.
  We also construct complete manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose balls are uniformly almost $1$-Euclidean at every scale, but for which no single harmonic function can be transformed into a splitting function at all smaller scales which give a negative answer to the existence question for all-scale splitting functions in \cite{HH}.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Transitive permutation groups with trivial four point stabilizers"
papers.authors: Paula H\"ahndel, Christoph M\"oller, Rebecca Waldecker
papers.abstract: This article revisits earlier work by the last author together with Kay Magaard. We correct mistakes in results about the Sylow 2- and 3-structure of groups that act with fixity 3 and one result about possible components, we improve some results and we add details.

papers.title: On Congruences modulo powers of 3 for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partitions in $k$-Colors
papers.authors: Anjelin Mariya Johnson, S. N. Fathima

papers.title: On Lagrangians of Oakley-Usher type
papers.abstract: The main theme of this paper is to study symplectic (un-)knottedness of Lagrangian submanifolds which are not tori. Our construction of such Lagrangians is inspired by the generalized Polterovich Lagrangians of Oakley--Usher and relies on an adaptation of symplectic reduction methods going back to Chekanov--Schlenk and McDuff's probes to the case of non-abelian group actions. We compare Oakley--Usher Lagrangians to their (un-)knotted cousins to find that, depending on the situation, they are: (1) not diffeomorphic, (2) diffeomorphic, but not Lagrangian isotopic, (3) Lagrangian isotopic, but not Hamiltonian isotopic, (4) Hamiltonian isotopic. This relationship between them frequently changes when the ambient space is compactified by a symplectic cut. In the companion paper "Lagrangian tori in the three-dimensional quadric and mirror symmetry", we focus on monotone tori in the three-dimensional quadric and compute their enumerative invariants and study their relationship to mirror symmetry.

papers.title: Divisor moments of polynomials in Fourier coefficients of modular forms
papers.abstract: We study higher moments of the divisor function evaluated at polynomial expressions in the Fourier coefficients of a non-CM newform. The logarithmic exponent appearing in our estimates depends only on the number of irreducible factors of the polynomial and remains unchanged under a Sato--Tate restriction. The proof combines an effective Chebotarev theorem, or an effective Chebotarev--Sato--Tate theorem, with the arithmetic of joint cycle types and a mean value estimation for multivariable multiplicative functions with Frobenian support.

papers.title: Mersenne Representation, the Conolly Sequence, and Soliton Profiles over Finite Fields
papers.abstract:
We study the canonical skew-binary representation of nonnegative integers, whose positional weights are the Mersenne numbers \(2^{k}-1\), and its decomposition into the binary and nonbinary sides. The nonbinary values, arranged in increasing order, form the OEIS sequence A055938, and their successor structure gives a direct proof of the relation with the OEIS sequence A080578 that is recorded as conjectural in the OEIS entry for A080578. The resulting formulas show that the Conolly sequence describes both sides of the decomposition: a shifted Conolly sequence is the counting function of the binary side, while the same sequence gives the increasing enumeration of the nonbinary side.
  We then develop the parent map, truncation blocks, truncation remainders, and the Mersenne tau function associated with this representation. The parent map is conjugate to deletion of the lowest digit. Differences of the Mersenne tau rows recover the parent iterates and the counting function, and they give formulas for digit reconstruction and for a diagonal tau defect.
  Finally, we revisit a known finite-depth one-soliton family of the finite-field BBS. The Mersenne combinatorics is used directly to reconstruct a global integer-valued traveling-wave profile and to prove an integer window-counting theorem. Reduction modulo \(3\) yields the corresponding finite-field traveling-wave solutions. We also construct an integer-valued traveling-wave tau function whose front values are given by the Mersenne tau rows. The resulting construction shows how the combinatorics of a number representation can enter directly into the reconstruction of solutions of an integrable system.

papers.title: Topological Rigidity of Contractible 3-Manifolds and Handlebody Interiors under Nonnegative Scalar Curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that a contractible $3$-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature is diffeomorphic to $\R^3$. We also prove that, if the interior of a compact handlebody of genus $\gamma$ admits such a metric, then $\gamma\leq1$. This answers two open questions posed by Wang and Gromov, respectively.

papers.title: Incidence algebras and beyond: brick-continuity and generic bricks
papers.abstract: We will show that the twelve families of minimally representation-infinite incidence algebras are brick-continuous and admit a generic brick, which will be explicitly constructed. After that, reversing the reduction process between posets, we will show that any representation-infinite incidence algebra is brick-continuous and admits a generic brick, which can be explicitly computed using what will be called ''extension functors''. Lastly, a method to apply these results to a broader class of algebras is given.

papers.title: Contact Surgery Numbers of the 3-torus
papers.abstract: We study contact surgery numbers for contact structures on the 3-torus. We show that all contact structures obtained via contact surgery along a Legendrian Borromean ring are overtwisted, and that this construction yields infinitely many pairwise non-contactomorphic contact structures on $\mathbb{T}^3$. We prove an obstruction on the maximal Thurston-Bennequin invariant of 3-component links to produce $\mathbb{T}^3$ by Dehn surgery. We also compare Legendrian surgery presentations of the Stein-fillable contact structure on $\mathbb{T}^3$. In this setting, we exhibit a non-destabilizable Legendrian knot with no graded normal ruling whose associated Stein filling has nonzero full symplectic homology.

papers.title: Optimal Oracle Complexity for Weakly Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the oracle complexity of finding $\epsilon$-stationary points of $\rho$-weakly convex and $G$-Lipschitz functions, where stationarity is measured by the gradient of the Moreau envelope. We consider an exact first-order oracle that returns both the function value and the full subdifferential at every query point. In the principal parameter regime, we prove that every first-order algorithm, including randomized algorithms, requires $\Omega(\tfrac{\rho G^2\Delta}{\epsilon^4})$ oracle queries to succeed with any fixed positive probability, where $f(0)-\inf f\le\Delta$. This lower bound matches the best known deterministic and stochastic first-order upper bounds, up to universal constants, and establishes the optimal randomized first-order oracle complexity. The result separates smooth nonconvex and weakly convex optimization: the additional $\epsilon^{-2}$ factor is intrinsic to nonsmooth geometry rather than stochastic oracle noise.

papers.title: The maximum volume polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the sphere
papers.abstract: A classical problem in convex and discrete geometry asks for the convex polyhedron of greatest volume whose vertices are chosen from the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$. For a prescribed number $N$ of vertices, the problem is known only in a small number of cases, namely $4\leq N\leq 8$ and $N=12$. In the case $N=9$, Wimmer showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the volume maximizer must be combinatorially equivalent to a triaugmented triangular prism. In this note, we complete the proof by determining the volume maximizer among all inscribed polytopes which are combinatorially equivalent to a triaugmented triangular prism. Consequently, every convex polyhedron with at most nine vertices on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has volume at most $3\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}-3}$, with equality, up to rotation, precisely for the ``symmetric'' triaugmented triangular prism whose vertex coordinates we compute exactly.

papers.title: Schwarzian Residue of the Samuelson Obstruction in Tangent Lagrangian 2-Webs
papers.abstract:
The Samuelson condition, a classical area-ratio condition for planar Lagrangian $2$-webs, is equivalent in local web coordinates $(u,v)$ to $\partial_u\partial_v\log|J_F(u,v)|=0$, where $F$ is the inverse web-coordinate map and $J_F$ is its Jacobian. For the tangent-line family $L_t: y=tx+h(t)$, with $h$ smooth on an open interval, let $\Psi(u,v)$, for $u
eq v$, be the intersection map of $L_u$ and $L_v$, write $J_{\Psi}$ for its Jacobian, and set $S_h(u,v) := \partial_u\partial_v\log|J_{\Psi}(u,v)|$ where $J_{\Psi}(u,v)
eq0$. Near each diagonal point $(t_0,t_0)$ with $h''(t_0)
eq0$, the obstruction admits the decomposition $S_h(u,v) =  rac{1}{(v-u)^2} + R_h(u,v)$, where $R_h$ extends smoothly across the diagonal near $(t_0,t_0)$. The universal pole yields $S_h(u,v)>0$ off the diagonal in a sufficiently small neighborhood of $(t_0,t_0)$, so the tangent web does not satisfy the Samuelson condition there. We call $R_h(t,t)$ the Schwarzian residue and show that $R_h(t,t) =  rac{1}{2}\{\sigma,t\} = -\kappa_{\mathrm{aff}}(\sigma) \left( rac{d\sigma}{dt}ight)^2$. Here $\sigma$ is the equi-affine arclength parameter of the envelope $\gamma(t)=(-h'(t),h(t)-t h'(t))$, and $\{\sigma,t\}$ denotes the Schwarzian derivative of $\sigma$ with respect to $t$. The equi-affine curvature $\kappa_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is defined by $\gamma_{\sigma\sigma\sigma}+\kappa_{\mathrm{aff}}\gamma_\sigma=0$. We also derive the transformation law of the residue under reparametrization of the tangent-line family.

papers.title: Static Equilibria of Perturbed Spheres: A Single-Harmonic Class Map, a Parity Obstruction, and a Certified Counter for the Mono-Monostatic Regime
papers.abstract: Varkonyi and Domokos proved that homogeneous convex bodies with any prescribed numbers $S\ge1$ of stable and $U\ge1$ of unstable static equilibria exist, the case $S=U=1$ being the mono-monostatic Gomboc. We give a complete constructive answer for the simplest nondegenerate shapes: a homogeneous body whose boundary is the unit sphere perturbed radially by a single real spherical harmonic $Y_\ell^m$ of degree $\ell\ge2$ and order $1\le m\le\ell$ has exactly $S=U=m(\ell-m+1)$ stable and unstable equilibria, for every amplitude in the convex range when $m\ge2$, and for small amplitude when $m=1$. The reduction to the critical points of the perturbing harmonic is an identity when $m\ge2$: the symmetry of a single tesseral harmonic pins the centroid at the origin exactly, so the centroid-to-surface distance is a strictly increasing function of the harmonic. We count the critical points of $Y_\ell^m$ from its separable structure and verify the Poincare-Hopf balance in index form. Three consequences follow. (i) A single harmonic populates only the diagonal $S=U$ of the equilibrium-class lattice; no single harmonic of degree $\ge2$ is mono-monostatic. (ii) Any centrally symmetric (even-degree) perturbation has even $S$ and $U$ and cannot be mono-monostatic, a parity obstruction. (iii) Mono-monostaticity is therefore intrinsically multi-harmonic. A predict-then-confirm numerical study on eight single-harmonic bodies matches the formula exactly. For the multi-harmonic regime we give a certified equilibrium counter (interval arithmetic with Krawczyk uniqueness and Hessian classification) that, given the centroid, provably neither under- nor over-counts. It certifies that a member of a known analytic family, at an amplitude of our own choosing inside the strictly convex sub-regime, is mono-monostatic. For that body the centroid is exactly the origin, so its certificate is unconditional.

papers.title: Equi-dependence implying independence
papers.abstract: It is shown that, if an event $A$ has the same conditional probability in each trial in an infinite sequence of Bernoulli trials, then $A$ is independent of each trial. More general results are actually established.

papers.title: Nearly balanced spanning subdivisions in dense digraphs
papers.abstract: Pavez-Sign\'e [Combin. Probab. Comput. 33 (2024), 121--128] conjectured a Dirac-type condition for spanning $H$-subdivisions and asked whether the subdivision paths can additionally be required to have similar lengths. Lee [European J. Combin. 124 (2025), 104059] resolved the existence conjecture in the stronger setting of digraphs. We answer the length-control question in this stronger directed setting: for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $C_0>0$ such that, for every digraph $H$ with $h$ arcs and no isolated vertices, every $n$-vertex digraph $D$ with $n\ge C_0h$ and $\delta^0(D)\ge(1/2+\varepsilon)n$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision whose subdivision paths have lengths differing by at most one.

papers.title: Spanning $H$-subdivisions with Prescribed Path Lengths
papers.abstract:
We study spanning $H$-subdivisions in dense graphs where the length of every subdivision path is prescribed in advance. This problem is motivated in part by a question of Pavez-Sign\'e [Combin. Probab. Comput. 33 (2024), 121--128], who asked whether the subdivision paths in a spanning $H$-subdivision can be required to have similar lengths.
  Let $h\ge3$ be an integer and let $0<\beta\ll\alpha\ll1/h$. We prove that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge n/2+\lfloor h/3\rfloor$ has the following property. For every graph $H$ with $h$ edges and no isolated vertices, write $E(H)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_h\}$, and every choice of integers $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_h\ge4$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^h\ell_i=n-|V(H)|+h$ and $\sum_{\ell_i<\alpha n}\ell_i\le\beta n$, the graph $G$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision in which the $i$th edge of $H$ is replaced by a path of length exactly $\ell_i$. We also give a family of examples showing that a linear additive term in $h$ is necessary in general.

papers.title: Sieve dimension and search depth for the Erd\H{o}s-Straus conjecture, $n \equiv 1 \pmod{24}$
papers.abstract: For primes $n\equiv1\pmod{24}$, we study the depth of explicit, factorization-free searches for a decomposition of $4/n$ into three positive unit fractions. Let $E_2(N;J)$ be the set of such primes $n\le N$ for which no coprime pair $1\le u,a\le J$ admits a divisor $s\mid an+u$ with $s\equiv-1\pmod{4ua}$. For every fixed $J$, we prove $|E_2(N;J)|\ll_J N/(\log N)^{1+A(J)/2}$, where $A(J)$ counts the coprime pairs in $[1,J]^2$. The proof uses a fixed-point-free involution and identifies the exact dimension of the covering. We also establish a dual Type I divisor criterion and an unconditional obstruction: at the fixed shift $c=7$, both branches of the cofactor criterion fail for $\asymp N/(\log N)^{3/2}$ primes. At growing depth, an exact reciprocal-totient asymptotic with leading constant $9/(2\pi^2)$ improves the explicit large-sieve bounds to $O(N\exp(-0.0942(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^5$, and to $O_\varepsilon(N\exp(-(0.1093-\varepsilon)(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^{4+\varepsilon}$ for fixed sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. Finally, combining a truncated Type I pass with a sparse residual search yields a complete, factorization-free batch decision procedure for all primes in $[N,2N]$, using $O(N^2(\log N)^2\exp(-c_0(\log N)^{2/3}))=o(N^2)$ arithmetic operations for some $c_0>0$. The conjecture itself remains open.

papers.title: Sharp Minimax Regret for Infinite-Memory Logistic Prediction
papers.abstract: We study sequential prediction of binary marks whose log-odds are a linear function of all past inputs. The inputs are independent uniform signs. The coefficient of the input observed $j$ steps earlier is unknown, but its absolute value is at most a known number $r_j$, and $\sum_j r_j\le B$. A learner is judged by its expected cumulative log loss in excess of the loss of the true conditional probabilities. We show that for every such sequence $r$ and every horizon $T$, the minimax value of this regret lies between $c\,\Gamma_T(r)/\max\{1,B^2\}$ and $\frac12\Gamma_T(r)$, where $\Gamma_T(r)=\sum_{j\le T}\log(1+(T-j+1)r_j^2)$ and $c$ is an absolute constant. The term for lag $j$ combines the size bound $r_j$ with the number $T-j+1$ of rounds in which that lag influences a prediction, and no monotonicity or other regularity of $r$ is needed. The upper bound is attained by a Bayesian mixture with independent Gaussian priors. For the lower bound, we apply the van Trees inequality at each prediction step and then bound the expected log-determinant of the random matrix whose rows are the lagged input vectors. We also characterize when $\frac12$ is the exact leading constant: for envelopes with a common bound $B$, possibly changing with $T$, the regret is asymptotic to $\frac12\Gamma_T(r)$ if and only if $\sum_{j\le T}\min\{1,(T-j+1)r_j^2\}=o(\Gamma_T(r))$. This gives, for example, $\log^2(A^2T)/(8\alpha)$ for $r_j=Ae^{-\alpha j}$, whereas for $r_j=Aj^{-s}$ with $s>1$ the regret is of order $T^{1/(2s)}$ and its ratio to $\Gamma_T(r)$ stays below $\frac12$. Finally, for a known horizon, an online Newton predictor with features scaled by $r_j$ attains regret of order $\Gamma_T(r)$ with polynomial computation per round.

papers.title: Selfless Reduced Crossed Product $C^{*}$-Algebras Arising from Almost Periodic Actions
papers.abstract: We prove that the reduced crossed product arising from an almost periodic action of an infinite countable discrete group on a unital, separable $C^*$-algebra is selfless whenever the crossed product is simple and monotracial and the group admits a topologically free extreme boundary action. We also give an alternative proof of a special case of a result of Gao, Junge, Kunnawalkam Elayavalli, Patchell, and Robert: the direct product of an exact $C^*$-simple group and a $C^*$-selfless group is $C^*$-selfless.

papers.title: Multiple ergodic averages for commuting multiplicative actions
papers.authors: Dimitrios Charamaras, Andreas Koutsogiannis, Konstantinos Tsinas
papers.abstract:
We study the convergence of multiple ergodic averages involving several commuting multiplicative actions. We prove that for finitely generated systems, the averages $$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N S_{1,n}F_1\cdot\ldots\cdot S_{\ell,n}F_\ell$$ converge in norm, settling a conjecture of Frantzikinakis.
  Our proofs feature tools from ergodic theory and probabilistic number theory. We exploit some stability properties of additive functions to establish a novel variant of \Katai's orthogonality criterion, which leads to box seminorm control for our averages. Using the theory of magic extensions introduced by Host and a delicate complexity reduction argument, we eventually reduce our problem to known convergence results.

papers.title: The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial: A Subgroup-Lattice Refinement
papers.abstract:
We introduce the multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomial F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}P_{\Gamma/h}(x,y), which aggregates the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials associated with all subgroups of a finite group acting on a graph. We derive the equivalent element-wise representation F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{g\in G}c_G(g)P_{\Gamma/g}(x,y), where c_G(g) = \sum_{\langle g\rangle\leq H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}. The coefficient function depends only on the cyclic subgroup generated by the element and is constant on conjugacy classes. This yields decompositions by cyclic subgroups and conjugacy classes and an interpretation in terms of the incidence algebra of the subgroup lattice. After normalization, the coefficients define a probability distribution obtained by choosing a subgroup uniformly and then an element uniformly from that subgroup. We also establish diagonal multiplicativity for disjoint unions and a weighted cycle-index expression for edgeless graphs.
  A further contribution concerns the distinguishing power of the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial. We answer a question of Dohmen and Lange-Geisler affirmatively by exhibiting two non-isomorphic graphs, P_3 and K_2 \mathbin{\dot\cup} K_1 under C_2-actions, with identical orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. The two actions nevertheless have different multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. Thus the multiorbital polynomial is not determined by the orbital bivariate polynomial, whereas the converse question remains open.

papers.title: Resolvent Estimates for the Stokes Operator in a Three-Dimensional Lipschitz Domain
papers.abstract:
By refining the approach developed in \cite{AGH-2015, GS2026a}, we establish resolvent estimates in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$ for the Stokes operator in a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ in $\R^3$ for $(3/2)-\e< p\le \infty$, where $\e>0$ depends on $\Omega$. As a consequence, the Stokes operator generates a uniformly bounded analytic semigroup in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$. The range for $p$ is sharp. The results are particularly surprising, as it is long believed that the $L^p$ resolvent estimates in three-dimensional Lipschitz domains may fail for large $p$.
  In the appendices we prove an interpolation theorem between $L^2_\sigma(\Omega)$ and $L^\infty_\sigma(\Omega)$. We also show that for $1< p< \infty$ and a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ in $\R^d, d\ge 2$, the resolvent estimate in $L^p(\Omega; \C^d)$ can hold only if the Helmholtz projection is bounded on this space. This explains the counter-example constructed in \cite{Deuring-2001}. Finally, we prove that the resolvent estimate may fail in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$ for $1< p< (3/2)$ and $d\ge 3$ as a consequence of failure of the Helmholtz decomposition of $L^p(\Omega; \C^d)$.

papers.title: Vertex interpolation by bivariate $C^1$ cubic splines: counterexamples, geometric stability, and indecomposable defects
papers.abstract: We study vertex evaluation on the full space of continuously differentiable piecewise cubic polynomials on a fixed planar triangulation. A complete dual description turns failure of interpolation into balanced edge weights with nonzero vertex loading. It leads to exact counterexamples with 17, 25, 31 and 41 vertices, each with one relation and the classical lower-bound dimension. The 31- and 41-vertex examples have interior graphs that are trees. We give a geometric construction criterion for a sector-completion family and a certified implicit construction outside that family. With all boundary vertices fixed, the nearby bad configurations form a four-dimensional smooth locus in the 17-vertex case, two intersecting components of dimensions six and five in the 25-vertex case, and isolated transverse points in the two tree examples. A common Schur-complement estimate explains their different interpolation costs. We first realize arbitrary defect by decomposable chains of the 41-vertex example. We then construct obstructions from individually interpolatory blocks, prove that the capacity of one complete edge is exactly five, and build a fixed-square family with arbitrarily large strongly indecomposable defect. The latter excludes two triangle-disjoint connected normal bad submeshes even when those submeshes may have holes.

papers.title: Fixed-Perimeter Franklin Statistics and an Eventual Inequality
papers.abstract: Gray, Payne, Swisher, and Watson conjectured that, for fixed integers $j \geq 0$ and $k \geq 2$, the number $FD_{j,k}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ having exactly $j$ part sizes of multiplicity at least $k$ is eventually at least the number $FO_{j,k}(n)$ having exactly $j$ distinct occurring part sizes divisible by $k$. We derive bivariate generating functions for both statistics using the profile-word encoding of a partition. For $k \geq 3$, coefficient extraction shows that fixing $j$ changes the order of the dominant pole but not its location. The corresponding dominant singularities are positive real numbers $\rho_k$ and $\sigma_k$, where $\rho_k$ satisfies $\rho_k+\rho_k^2+\cdots+\rho_k^k=1$ and $\sigma_k$ satisfies $\sigma_k^k=(1-\sigma_k)^{k-1}$. We prove that $\rho_k<\sigma_k$ for every $k \geq 3$. Consequently, $FD_{j,k}(n)/FO_{j,k}(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, proving the conjecture and yielding a strict eventual inequality for $k \geq 3$. The case $k=2$ recovers the known exact identity.

papers.title: The Gaussian Multiuser Channel Capacity Region
papers.abstract: This work characterizes a Gaussian multiuser-channel capacity-region using receiver-subset message atoms, Gaussian single-user equivalents, and successive decoding. A memoryless multiuser-channel model specifies both the channel conditional distribution and the independent-use input distribution. For all linear Gaussian channels, independent Gaussian user signaling and receiver-local worst-case-noise/MMSE-GDFE transformations provide a single-user-equivalent basis for the complete capacity-region construction. Each user distributes its input autocorrelation among a finite set of receiver-subset atoms, whose rate sums satisfy the applicable receiver constraints. Minimum-energy and weighted-rate-sum designs optimize these allocations, while fixed-allocation linear programs determine feasible atomic rates and synchronized time-shared successive-decoding implementations. The resulting framework includes Gaussian multiple-access, broadcast, and interference channels, with numerical examples illustrating their rate regions and receiver designs.

papers.title: Projective Rigidity of $U(k)$-Radial Ricci-Flat K\"ahler Metrics
papers.abstract: We study K\"ahler immersions of Ricci-flat metrics into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space. Let $L^{\otimes k}\simeq K_X$ over a real-analytic K\"ahler manifold $X$. Let $\phi$ be a base potential and $s$ the canonical squared fibre norm on $L^{\oplus k}$. Consider Ricci-flat potentials $\phi+h(s)$ near the zero section, with $h$ independent of the base point. We prove that local projective inducibility forces the base to be Ricci-flat and the metric to split locally as $X\times\mathbb C^k$. In that case projective inducibility is equivalent to that of the base. The proof combines Calabi's criterion, positivity of the homogeneous fibre-degree blocks, and the singularities of the radial profile. A related obstruction along holomorphic curves excludes every positive multiple of the Taub--NUT metric and Calabi's hyperk\"ahler metrics on $T^{*1,0}\mathbb{CP}^n$. Applications also include the resolved conifold, canonical-bundle metrics in non-Einstein classes, and Cifarelli's rank-two Type-2 metric.

papers.title: The proper geometric dimension of the mapping class groups of non-orientable surfaces with punctures
papers.authors: Nestor Colin, Rita Jim\'enez Rolland, Porfirio L. Le\'on \'Alvarez, Luis Jorge S\'anchez Salda\~na
papers.abstract: We study the proper geometric dimension of {\it full} mapping class groups of non-orientable surfaces with punctures. Building on the computation for closed non-orientable surfaces, we prove that the proper geometric dimension agrees with the virtual cohomological dimension in all but a finite collection of low-complexity cases, for which we obtain explicit bounds. Our results provide the non-orientable counterpart of the corresponding computations for mapping class groups of closed and punctured orientable surfaces.

papers.title: Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
papers.abstract: All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.

papers.title: Geometric Detection and Finiteness of Log Crystalline Local Systems
papers.abstract: We prove a geometric detection theorem for log crystalline local systems in the smooth proper setting with a normal crossings boundary. The associated special-fiber log $F$-isocrystal detects geometric absolute irreducibility and, modulo constant rank-one twists, determines the pullback to the geometric generic fiber. The main ingredient is a determinant argument combining a finite-order rank-one reduction, logarithmic period comparison, and the Pl\"ucker embedding. As an application, using Abe--Esnault's finiteness theorem and finiteness of stable lattices, we prove finiteness, up to geometrically constant rank-one twists, of geometrically absolutely irreducible log crystalline local systems of fixed rank. Coefficients may lie in any fixed finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, and no bound on the Hodge--Tate weights is imposed.

papers.title: Asymptotic quasi--local structure induced by Magnetic field
papers.abstract: We introduce a magnetic coherent--state frame over the Landau levels of the two--dimensional Landau Hamiltonian, indexed by a discrete metric space combining spatial and energy degrees of freedom. Although overcomplete, the frame is almost--orthogonal, and we use it to endow the CAR $C^*$--algebra over the one--particle Hilbert space with an \emph{asymptotic quasi--local} (AQL) structure, in which graded commutators of observables localized on disjoint index sets decay exponentially rather than vanish exactly. By means of a family of conditional expectations onto the resulting local subalgebras, we construct a Fr\'echet $*$--subalgebra of almost--local observables, invariant under the discrete group of lattice translations, which act on it by continuous automorphisms. For the full continuous group of magnetic translations we establish a quantitative control on how local observables spread through this almost--local algebra, and we show that this control suffices to extend graded asymptotic abelianness from the lattice to the entire continuous translation group. The results provide a discrete--continuum dictionary intended as the starting point for extending Lieb--Robinson--type techniques from lattice systems to interacting continuum electrons in a magnetic field.

papers.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
papers.authors: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng
papers.abstract:
We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$.
  Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$.
  We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.

papers.title: Multiplicity-Weighted Moments of a Two-Monomial Harmonic Map Beyond the Caustic
papers.abstract: While the Jacobian of a planar harmonic mapping keeps a constant sign, the signed and the unsigned area elements agree up to that sign, and the two natural moment hierarchies coincide. Once the Jacobian changes sign the critical circle acquires a caustic as its image, part of the plane is covered several times with opposite orientations, and the hierarchies part company: integrating a radial weight against $J_F$ lets overlapping sheets cancel, giving the degree-weighted moments $J_n$, while integrating against $|J_F|$ lets every sheet count positively, giving the multiplicity-weighted moments $J_n^{\pm}$. These are the classical degree and area formulas for the same map, the second weighted by the multiplicity function (Banach indicatrix). It is the second family, the one the caustic threatens, for which a closed form is no longer automatic. For the two-monomial map $F(w)=w+iC\bar w^{k}$ on an annulus we show that it has one anyway: $J_n^{\pm}$ is the total variation of the very same explicit primitive whose endpoint difference gives $J_n$. Crossing the caustic therefore costs exactly one extra evaluation point, the critical radius $r_*=(k|C|)^{-1/(k-1)}$, and it is the same point for every order $n$: the weight $|F|^{2n}$ is nonnegative and so contributes no sign change of its own. On the degree-weighted side $J_n$ has a boundary-only closed form for every $n\ge0$, the zeroth being the signed area of the image counted with degree, and the complex-weighted moments vanish unless $(k+1)\mid(m-\ell)$. Neither weighted integral is a new object, and the caustic of this family has been located before in the literature on harmonic trinomials; what is new is the closed evaluation of the multiplicity-weighted hierarchy across it.

papers.title: Structure of derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings
papers.abstract: In this article, we study derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings regarded as discrete rings. We compare each such algebra with the degreewise inverse limit of the derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in finite rings and with its subalgebra consisting of elements with uniformly finite double-coset support. Under cohomological comparison hypotheses, the natural map to this subalgebra has image given by its degree-zero part and its positive-degree torsion. We describe the kernel in terms of continuous cohomology and prove that it is a divisible square-zero ideal annihilated by every positive-degree element. These comparisons are compatible with Yoneda products, and the action on torsion Ext classes factors through the image. We compute the resulting algebras for the additive group $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and determine the underlying graded abelian groups for $(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p),\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}_p))$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p>3$. The examples exhibit distinct effects of the coefficient topology and the support condition.

papers.title: Aigner's majorization conjecture in quantitative group testing: counterexamples and eventual sufficiency for star forests
papers.abstract: We refute Aigner's majorization conjecture for star forests in adaptive quantitative group testing with two defective items. Each test counts the defectives in a chosen subset; the possible defective pairs form the edges of a star forest. Aigner's necessary majorization condition is sufficient through five tests but is not sufficient at any budget from six onward. Nevertheless, for every fixed number of stars, it becomes sufficient once the test budget is large enough. We prove that majorization is sufficient for all forests with at most twenty-nine stars, and that this bound is sharp. We also construct counterexamples that pass arbitrarily many successive compatibility checks based on majorization. The five-test converse, counterexamples, eventual sufficiency theorem and unbounded-delay construction have analytic proofs. The sharp finite support bounds also use exact integer-inequality certificates.

papers.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.

papers.title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
papers.abstract: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.

papers.title: Boundary-layer separation beyond the square-root law
papers.authors: Ky Giao Duong, Tej-Eddine Ghoul, Sameer Iyer, Yasunori Maekawa
papers.abstract:
We construct solutions to the two-dimensional stationary Prandtl system under a constant adverse pressure gradient exhibiting a family of distinct separation laws. More precisely, for every integer $\ell\ge1$, we construct smooth initial data for which separation occurs at a finite location $x=x^\ast$, with
  \[
  \partial_y u(x,0)
  =\mathbf C_\ell(x^\ast-x)^{\ell/2}\bigl(1+o(1)\bigr),
  \qquad x\uparrow x^\ast,
  \]
  where $\mathbf C_\ell>0$ depends on the initial data. We determine the local asymptotic structure of the solution near separation through matched inner and outer expansions based on linearization around the ground state in von Mises variables. This description addresses Open Problem~5 proposed by Oleinik and Samokhin~\cite{OleinikSamok-book-99}. We prove the nonlinear stability of the square-root separation law ($\ell=1$) under small admissible perturbations of the initial data in a suitable topology.

papers.title: Cubic arithmetic-geometric mean and isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves
papers.abstract: We construct degree-three isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic different from three, which correspond to a step of the cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. As an application, we describe the Serre-Tate canonical lift of an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic three by the 3-adic cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. We also discuss the relations of the Hesse curves with complex and finite hypergeometric functions.

papers.title: Betti Numbers of Odd Biisotropic Symplectic Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We compute the singular cohomology groups of odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ by presenting an explicit dimension-preserving combinatorial bijection between the Bialynicki-Birula cells in $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ and the Schubert cells in $\operatorname{Gr}(k, 2n+2-k)$.

papers.title: A Dubnov-Ivanov-Nagata-Higman Theorem for NIP nilrings
papers.authors: Christian d'Elb\'ee, Yanis Davoust, Jules Tindzogho Ntsiri
papers.abstract: We prove that NIP nilrings of bounded nilexponent are nilpotent. We also deduce that NIP $\omega$-categorical $n$-Engel Lie algebras of characteristic $p>n$ are nilpotent, yielding a case of the Lie algebra analogous of Wilson conjecture for $\omega$-categorical groups.

papers.title: Amortized Score-Hamiltonian Policy Iteration: A Grid-Free Scheme for Relaxed Stochastic Control Problems
papers.abstract: We develop an amortized, grid-free implementation of continuous Langevin dynamics based policy-value iteration for entropy-regularized, infinite-horizon relaxed stochastic control problems. The improvement rate of the exact iteration is a discounted aggregate of relative Fisher information between the policy and the Gibbs law of its Hamiltonian. The associated score residual is the velocity with which the control's Langevin dynamics transport its law. We project this velocity onto a conditional sampler shared across states, instead of one Langevin dynamics per state, and the value dynamics onto a parametric critic, estimating both projections at sampled states to obtain coupled actor--critic flows. The score loss measures the actor's agreement with the current critic, while the policy-evaluation residual measures the critic's agreement with the actor. We also derive gradient and Hessian residuals, including a Feynman--Kac representation for the gradient equation, to control errors not detected by the projected value iteration. An exact decomposition of the HJB residual combines these errors into a policy-suboptimality bound under verification and logarithmic Sobolev assumptions. In the linear-quadratic class, both projections are exact and recover the pointwise iteration, and we provide numerical experiments on general models to demonstrate the coupled actor--critic learning in high-dimensions.

papers.title: Logarithmic upper bounds and axial front selection for spatially periodic lattice Fisher--KPP equations
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=\Delta_{\Z^d}u+F(x,u)$ on $\Z^d$ ($d\geq2$) with a spatially periodic Fisher--KPP reaction $F$ and a nonzero, finitely supported initial datum $u_0:\Z^d\to[0,1]$. We establish a logarithmic upper bound on the front position that holds uniformly in the observation direction, with a logarithmic delay coefficient governed by the outward normal to the asymptotic spreading body. When the linearized growth rate $F_s(x,0)$ is independent of the longitudinal coordinate, we prove the matching axial Bramson correction and show that the solution converges uniformly on fixed-width half-tubes to a critical pulsating front up to a bounded, slowly varying phase shift. For critical pulsating profiles $\Phi(s,x)$ satisfying $\Phi(s,x)\leq C(1+s)\ee^{-\lambda s}$ for $s\geq0$ and $x\in\Z^d$, where $\lambda>0$ is the critical spatial decay rate, we derive the precise leading-edge asymptotic expansion and prove uniqueness up to translation. As a consequence, in the axial regime we obtain sharp asymptotics for the arrival times $T_\theta(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:u(t,x)\geq\theta\}$ ($0<\theta<1$), including the asymptotic time lag between distinct level sets at a remote site and the period-to-period passage time along the axis. For general periodic linearized growth rates, we introduce a nonlinear subsolution built from a positive quotient of linear Dirichlet evolutions on a retreating domain and formulate sufficient kernel estimates for a matching directional lower bound.

papers.title: Seifert type magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains
papers.abstract: We construct magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains whose magnetic lines define an $(m,n)$ Seifert fibration for arbitrary coprime integers $m,n$.

papers.title: Local Characterizations of Oka Manifolds
papers.authors: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie
papers.abstract:
We prove that strong dominability, the LAP, and the Oka property are equivalent for complex manifolds. The proof turns approximation across an attached disc in one complex variable, uniformly in holomorphic parameters, into convex approximation in arbitrary dimension. We also characterize Oka manifolds by the LEP, formulated in terms of centered holomorphic families of discs.
  In dimension $n\geq1$, LEP propagates across sets of zero $(2n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. The Oka property is local in the Euclidean topology, and it descends under surjective holomorphic maps between connected complex manifolds.
  Deformations of very free rational curves give the Oka property for every smooth connected complex projective rationally connected manifold $X$, and for $X\setminus A$ whenever $A\subset X$ is a closed algebraic subset of codimension at least two. Compact K\"ahler manifolds admitting a K\"ahler metric with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature, or having nef tangent bundle, are also Oka. For $n\geq1$, the complement of a smooth hypersurface $D\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ is Oka if and only if $d\leq n+1$.

papers.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
papers.authors: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, David Kruzel, Michael Lacey, Amelia Stokolosa

papers.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction across Smoothness and Noise Conditions
papers.authors: Wei Jiang, Yibo Wang, Sifan Yang, Lijun Zhang, Zechao Li
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study adaptive stochastic non-convex optimization under unknown smoothness and noise conditions. Our algorithms require no smoothness constant, noise bound, initial function gap, or oracle-regime label. We first propose a fixed-budget method that combines normalized momentum, recursive variance reduction, and a fresh gradient stage, followed by fresh validation of the candidates. We prove that the same output has expected gradient norm $O(T^{-1/4})$ under objective smoothness and bounded noise variance, $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ for noiseless gradients, where $T$ counts individual gradient evaluations.
  We then develop an anytime algorithm whose three optimization paths preserve their endpoints across reporting and budget-extension boundaries. The same three rates hold at every deterministic query budget, although the algorithm receives no information about the budget $T$. The analysis combines a scale potential, a uniform second-moment bound, and accounting for candidates retained through unfinished blocks. An optional sample-mean selector further reduces cumulative validation work from $O(T)$ to $O(T^{2/3})$ while preserving these rates.

papers.title: Initialization-Dependent Solution Selection by the Euler-Maruyama Scheme for a Degenerate SDE
papers.abstract: We study the Euler-Maruyama approximation of the degenerate stochastic differential equation $dX_t = |X_t|^\alpha\,dW_t$, $0 < \alpha < 1/2$, $X_0 = 0$, for which uniqueness in law fails. The Euler scheme started exactly from zero is trapped by the absorbing solution, whereas a nonzero initialization $x_h \to 0$ can select a different weak solution. We identify the initialization-dependent limiting regimes. The critical spatial scale is $r_h = h^{1/[2(1-\alpha)]}$, and the relevant depth parameter is $\Theta_h = h\log(1+\log^+(r_h/|x_h|))$. If $\Theta_h \to 0$, the scheme converges to the non-sticky weak solution. If $\Theta_h \to \theta \in (0,\infty)$, it converges to the solution that stays at zero for the deterministic time $\theta/|\log\alpha|$ and then evolves as the non-sticky solution. If $\Theta_h \to \infty$, the scheme converges to the absorbing solution. The proof is based on an exact scale-invariant Euler chain, a logarithmic exit-time law of large numbers, a discrete Tanaka occupation estimate, and a compact-uniform restart argument. Every finite deterministic delay can be obtained by a suitable vanishing initialization, while oscillating depth parameters yield process-level nonconvergence. Thus a vanishing initialization can survive in the limit as a macroscopic deterministic delay and thereby act as a solution selector for the Euler-Maruyama approximation.

papers.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
papers.authors: Gordon Heier, Ravi Mudaliar, Haotian Zuo
papers.abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

papers.title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
papers.abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.

papers.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras
papers.abstract:
We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic.
  The proof that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial uses the rational models for the Becker--Gottlieb and THH transfers obtained in previous work of the authors. In the appendix, we provide a second, more involved proof that relies on constructing explicit $C_\infty$-algebra models for odd spherical fibrations (including circle bundles), which might be of independent interest.
  Concurrently, another counterexample (of a very different flavor) was found by Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, and the first author.

papers.title: Descending Everest, Part I: Oracle Complexity of Convex Optimization under $(L_0,L_1)$-Smoothness
papers.authors: Mikhail Rudomanov, Ivan Fomin, Alexander V. Gasnikov, Fedor S. Stonyakin
papers.abstract: For convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth functions, the curvature may grow together with the gradient norm. Therefore, even when $\|x^0-x^*\|\le R$, the gradient and the optimality gap at the starting point may be exponentially large in $L_1R$, and the bound $\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}$, known for the accelerated method on functions with Lipschitz gradient, no longer describes the complexity of the problem. We determine the oracle complexity of this class for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: for $L_0R^2/\varepsilon\ge1$, the optimal number of oracle calls $N$ satisfies $1+N=\widetilde\Theta(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+L_1R)$. The upper bound reads $O(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(1+L_1R)\log(2+L_1R))$: the method first passes through the large-gradient regime in $O(1+L_1R)$ iterations with an inexact line search, and then the standard accelerated method with a constant stepsize takes over. The lower bound is obtained by means of chains and the orthogonal invariance principle on functions conjugate to strongly convex functions on a polytope. If the initial optimality gap is at most $4\varepsilon$, the optimal bound becomes $1+N=\widetilde\Theta(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(L_1R)^{2/3})$.

papers.title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
papers.abstract: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework leveraging knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix up to a linear transformation. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

papers.title: Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.

papers.title: All totally real abelian number fields of class number one are Euclidean
papers.abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean. By referring to an additional announced uniform zero-free half-plane for general Dedekind zeta functions, we also establish the corresponding result for certain explicit new families of non-Galois cubic, quartic and quintic fields of unit rank one or two.

papers.title: From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.

papers.title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose and study a multi-labeling generalization of the $k$-radio labeling problem of graphs: given a graph $G$ and integers $k$ and $m$, assign to each vertex of $G$ a set of $m$ integer labels such that distinct labels assigned to a vertex differ by at least $k+1$, and the labels of any two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ pairwise differ by at least $k+1-d(x,y)$, with $d(x,y)$ being the distance between vertices $x$ and $y$. We prove general bounds on the minimum span of such a labeling and more refined results for the case $k=1$. For paths and cycles, we derive sharp bounds on the minimum span when $k$ is small. We finally propose a conjecture for the minimum span on the path and for an almost-tight bound on the cycle.

papers.title: Scattering in spacetime cones for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.authors: Andrew Hassell, Qiuye Jia, Xiaoxu Wu
papers.abstract:
We consider the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$, with a class of `mixed' nonlinearities that admit soliton solutions. We are interested in the long-time behaviour of solutions with finite, but possibly large, mass and/or energy. By a spacetime cone, we mean an open set in $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}_{x,t}$ that is invariant under dilation $(x, t) \mapsto (\alpha x, \alpha t)$ for all $\alpha > 0$.
  Our main result is as follows: let $u(x, t)$ be the solution with initial condition in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Let $\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}$ be the mass and energy of $u$, and let $\eta = \eta(\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}) > 0$ be sufficiently small. Let $C_\epsilon$ be the complement of $N \geq 1$ of sufficiently thin spacetime cones $\{ (x, t) \mid |x-v_jt| \leq \epsilon t \}$, where $v_1, \dots, v_N$ are fixed velocities and $\epsilon$ is sufficiently small. If the $L^\infty$ norm of $u$ in $C_\epsilon$ is $\leq \eta$, we prove that $u$ scatters in $C_{2\epsilon} \subset C_\epsilon$.

papers.title: SAT Solving by Multiplication in and Addition out of Clauses
papers.abstract: In this article, we use the PBNF-transform, or Polynomial Boolean Normal Form, described in the two earlier articles and now extended to higher arity, to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (SAT), which are part of the P versus NP problem. SAT consists of a conjunction of clauses, and in our SAT-solving models, we dualize the logical equations by inverting the problem: we multiply letters (literals) in the transferred clauses and use a binary iterated composition based on adding polynomials for the conjunctions in our solution formula. We obtain Polynomial Boolean Equations, PBE=0, by also renaming the truth value T=0. With reversed literal repetition, we get the CNF as the sum of the transformed clauses. In fact, we can always reduce to multiplication in and addition out of clauses, as we do not look for the entire kernel of PBE for a YES instance for SAT.

papers.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
papers.abstract: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $\alpha$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($\alpha = 0)$ and the SQG equation $(\alpha = 1)$. We prove that, for every $\alpha \in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$. The proof has been formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
papers.abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

papers.title: Weakly Unitary Zeon Matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, zeon matrix groups are discussed for the first time. Extending the concept of unitary complex matrices (i.e., matrices $A$ such that $A^\dagger A=\mI$) to matrices having entries in the complex zeon algebra $\CZ$, a ``zeon dagger'' operator $\zdag$ is defined and used to declare a zeon matrix $\Xi$ to be {\em unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI$. The unitary zeon matrices of order $n$ form a subgroup $\U_n$ of all invertible order-$n$ zeon matrices. A more interesting notion is that of ``weak unitarity'' of a zeon matrix. In particular, a zeon matrix $\Xi$ will be said to be {\em weakly unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI+\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a diagonal nilpotent zeon matrix. The weakly unitary matrices of order $n$ form a group $\W_n$, of which $\U_n$ is a subgroup. It is further shown that the exponential of a graph's nilpotent adjacency matrix has a natural orthogonal decomposition into the sum of a weakly unitary zeon matrix and a nilpotent zeon matrix. Eigenvalues of the weakly unitary zeon matrix reveal information about the graph's cycles and paths.

papers.title: Energy stability of explicit--implicit--null time discretizations for a class of nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients
papers.abstract: We study a class of nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients admitting a scalar energy potential. The explicit--implicit--null (EIN) method avoids severe time step restrictions of explicit time stepping and costly Newton--Raphson iterations required by a fully implicit treatment of the nonlinearity. Using orthogonal projection of the Kirchhoff transform, we prove nonlinear energy stability for first- to third-order EIN time stepping coupled with a wide range of spatial discretizations that admit self-adjoint positive semidefinite discrete operators. Under an upper bound for the diffusion coefficient on relevant stage segments, two IMEX coefficient conditions yield sufficient stabilization bounds without any time step restriction. The estimates dissipate the original convex energy and allow degenerate diffusion. We also extend the analysis to diffusion systems with a scalar energy potential in a fixed positive definite metric, and to consistent positive-weight quadrature discretizations. Applications include porous-medium flow, nonlinear heat transfer in plasma, and multicomponent diffusion.

papers.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The main result states that, under the assumption of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Based on this result, we also establish multilinear extrapolation of boundedness on rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and multilinear extrapolation of compactness on general Banach function spaces. Beyond that, we give characterizations of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on both general Banach function spaces and certain specific function spaces. All results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.

papers.title: Modular Existential Closedness
papers.abstract:
We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$.
  The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps.
